safi-cedvel:46-46.t:
* I'rab:
(الهمزة) is interrogative with the meaning of a command; (الفاء) is a conjunction; (في الأرض) is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (يسيروا); (الفاء) is the fāʾ of causation (fāʾ al-sababiyya); (تكون) is an incomplete (nāqiṣ), abrogating (nāsikh) imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by an implied (muḍmara) أن after the fāʾ; (لهم) is attached to a fronted khabar (predicate); (قلوب) is the noun (ism) of تكون, nominative (marfūʿ).
The interpreted maṣdar (al-maṣdar al-muʾawwal) (أن تكون..) is in the position of the nominative, conjoined (maʿṭūf) to a maṣdar (verbal noun) taken from the preceding speech, i.e.: "Is there any travelling in the land, so that there be understanding hearts ..." [Note: The rebuke may be by conjoining a negated thing to a negated thing, i.e.: "Is there an absence of travelling, and so an absence of understanding hearts.."].
(بها) is attached to (يعقلون), and the second (بها) is attached to (يسمعون); (الفاء) is causal (taʿlīliyya), and the pronoun in (إنّها) is the pronoun of the matter (ḍamīr al-shaʾn), the ism of inna; (لا) is negating; (الواو) is a conjunction; (لكن) is a particle of rectification (istidrāk), inoperative (muhmal); (التي) is a relative noun in the position of the nominative, a naʿt (adjective) of "the hearts"; (في الصدور) is attached to an omitted ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun التي ...
The clause «يسيروا ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to an implied resumptive clause, i.e.: "Were they heedless, so they did not travel" [Note: The fāʾ may be resumptive, and the clause يسيروا resumptive.].
The clause «تكون لهم قلوب ...» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the implied (muḍmar) particle-relative (al-mawṣūl al-ḥarfī) (أن).
The clause «يعقلون ...» is in the position of the nominative, a naʿt of قلوب.
The clause «يسمعون ...» is in the position of the nominative, a naʿt of آذان.
The clause «إنّها لا تعمى الأبصار ...» has no grammatical position, resumptive, carrying a sense of causation (taʿlīl).
The clause «لا تعمى الأبصار ...» is in the position of the nominative, the khabar of inna.
The clause «تعمى القلوب ...» is in the position of the nominative, conjoined to the khabar clause.

safi-cedvel:47-47.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) is resumptive (istiʾnāfiyya); (بالعذاب) is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (يستعجلونك).
(الواو) is a conjunction — or parenthetical (iʿtirāḍiyya); (عند) is an adverb (ẓarf), accusative (manṣūb), attached to a naʿt (adjective) of (يوما); (كألف) is attached to the khabar (predicate) of inna; (ما) is a maṣdar-forming particle (ḥarf maṣdarī)..
The interpreted maṣdar (ما تعدّون) is in the position of the genitive (majrūr), attached to a naʿt of (ألف سنة).

safi-cedvel:48-48.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) is resumptive (istiʾnāfiyya); (كأيّن من قرية أمليت): the i'rab of its parallel has already been given [Note: In verse (45) of this sūra.]; (الواو) is circumstantial (ḥāliyya); (إليّ) is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) a fronted khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ (subject) (المصير).
The clause «كأيّن من قرية) [Translator's note: the closing bracket is so in the source] has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «أمليت لها» is in the position of the nominative, the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (كأيّن).
The clause «هي ظالمة» is in the position of the accusative, a ḥāl (circumstantial).
The clause «أخذتها ...» is in the position of the nominative, conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause أمليت لها.
The clause «إليّ المصير» has no grammatical position, resumptive.

safi-cedvel:49-51.t:
* I'rab:
(أيّها) is the one addressed (munādā), an intended indefinite (nakira maqṣūda), indeclinable (mabnī) on the ḍamma, in the position of the accusative, and (ها) is for drawing attention (tanbīh); (الناس) is a badal (substitute) of أيّ — or an ʿaṭf bayān (explicative apposition) — following it in the nominative in form (lafẓan); (لكم) is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (نذير), the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ (subject) أنا.
The clause «قل ...» has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «the vocative and its response ...» is in the position of the accusative, the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl).
The clause «أنا لكم نذير ...» has no grammatical position, the response to the vocative.
(الفاء) is a conjunction of consequence (tafrīʿiyya); (الذين) is a relative noun, mubtadaʾ, in the position of the nominative; (لهم) is attached to an omitted fronted khabar of the mubtadaʾ (مغفرة).
The clause «الذين آمنوا ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the response to the vocative.
The clause «آمنوا ...» has no grammatical position, the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun (الذين).
The clause «عملوا ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the ṣila clause.
The clause «لهم مغفرة ...» is in the position of the nominative, the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (الذين).
(الواو) is a conjunction; (الذين) is a mubtadaʾ; (في آياتنا) is attached to (سعوا) by its being made to include (taḍmīn) the meaning of "they demolished", or "they strove to invalidate them"; (معاجزين) is a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the fāʿil (agent) of سعوا, accusative (manṣūb), the sign of its accusative being the yāʾ; (أولئك) is a demonstrative, mubtadaʾ, whose khabar is (أصحاب), nominative.
The clause «الذين سعوا ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause الذين آمنوا..
The clause «سعوا ...» has no grammatical position, the ṣila of the relative noun (الذين).
The clause «أولئك أصحاب ...» is in the position of the nominative, the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (الذين).

* Morphology:
(سعوا): it contains iʿlāl (weak-letter change) by deletion; its origin is سعاوا; two quiescent letters met, so the alif was deleted and the letter before the wāw was given fatḥa to indicate it; its pattern is فعوا with fatḥa on the fāʾ and the ʿayn.
(معاجزين): plural of معاجز, the active participle of the quadriliteral عاجز; its pattern is مفاعل with ḍamma on the mīm and kasra on the ʿayn.

safi-cedvel:52-54.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) is resumptive (istiʾnāfiyya); (من قبلك) is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (أرسلنا); (رسول) is genitive (majrūr) in form and accusative in position, a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); (لا) is redundant (zāʾida), to emphasise the negation; (نبيّ) is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to رسول in form, genitive; (إلّا) is a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr) [Note: Or a particle of exception, and the condition, its verb and its response are in the position of the accusative as a disjoined exception (istithnāʾ munqaṭiʿ); this is the choice of Abū al-Baqāʾ.]; (في أمنيّته) is attached to (ألقى) by its being made to include (taḍmīn) the meaning of "influenced" or "took control"; (الفاء) is a conjunction; (ما) is a maṣdar-forming particle (ḥarf maṣdarī) [Note: Or a relative noun, mafʿūl bihi, with the referent pronoun (ʿāʾid) omitted.]; (آياته) is a mafʿūl bihi, accusative (manṣūb), the sign of its accusative being the kasra.
The clause «ما أرسلنا ...» has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «the condition, its verb and its response» is in the position of the genitive — or of the accusative, according to the position (ʿalā al-maḥall) — a naʿt (adjective) of نبيّ [Note: al-Jamal permitted it to be in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) of نبيّ or of رسول.. but a conditional clause headed by (إذا) is weak in coming as a ḥāl.].
The clause «تمنّى ...» is in the position of the genitive, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct).
The clause «ألقى الشيطان ...» has no grammatical position, the apodosis of a non-jussive condition (jawāb sharṭ ghayr jāzim).
The clause «ينسخ الله ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the apodosis clause.
The clause «يلقي الشيطان ...» has no grammatical position, the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative (ما), the particle or the noun.
The interpreted maṣdar (al-maṣdar al-muʾawwal) (ما يلقي ...) is in the position of the accusative, a mafʿūl bihi. And the clause «يحكم الله ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause ينسخ الله.
The clause «الله عليم حكيم ...» has no grammatical position, a parenthetical resumption (istiʾnāf iʿtirāḍī).
(اللام) is for causation (taʿlīl), and the verb is accusative by an implied (muḍmara) أن after the lām, and the fāʿil (agent) is "He", i.e. Allah; (ما يلقي الشيطان) is like the first; (فتنة) is a second mafʿūl bihi, accusative; (للذين) is attached to a naʿt of فتنة; (في قلوبهم) is attached to a fronted khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ (subject) (مرض); (القاسية) is conjoined to the relative noun الذين by the wāw; (قلوبهم) is the fāʿil of the active participle القاسية, nominative (marfūʿ).
The interpreted maṣdar (أن يجعل ...) is in the position of the genitive by the lām, attached to (يحكم), or to (ينسخ).
(الواو) is resumptive; (اللام) is the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa), for emphasis; (في شقاق) is attached to the khabar of inna.
The clause «يجعل ...» has no grammatical position, the ṣila of the implied (muḍmar) particle-relative (al-mawṣūl al-ḥarfī) (أن).
The clause «يلقي الشيطان ...» has no grammatical position, the ṣila of the particle-relative (ما) or the nominal one.
The interpreted maṣdar (ما يلقي ...) is in the position of the accusative, a first mafʿūl bihi, its governor (ʿāmil) being يجعل.
The clause «في قلوبهم مرض ...» has no grammatical position, the ṣila of the relative noun (الذين).
The clause «إنّ الظالمين لفي شقاق ...» has no grammatical position, a parenthetical resumption.
(الواو) is a conjunction; (ليعلم) is like ليجعل; (أوتوا) is a passive past verb.. and (الواو) is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); (العلم) is a mafʿūl bihi, accusative; (من ربّك) is attached to a ḥāl of الحقّ; (الفاء) is a conjunction in both places; (يؤمنوا) is an imperfect verb, accusative, conjoined to يعلم.
The interpreted maṣdar (أن يعلم ...) is in the position of the genitive by the lām, attached to that to which the previous maṣdar (أن يجعل ...) is attached.
The interpreted maṣdar (أنّه الحق..) is in the position of the accusative, standing in place of the two objects of يعلم.
(له) is attached to (تخبت); (الواو) is resumptive; (اللام) is the shifted lām, for emphasis; (هاد) is the khabar of inna, nominative, the sign of its nominative being the ḍamma implied (muqaddara) on the yāʾ which is omitted in writing [Note: Because it drops in reading when continuing (waṣlan), or to suit the reading with tanwīn.]; (الذين) is a relative noun in the position of the genitive, muḍāf ilayhi; (إلى صراط) is attached to (هادي).
The clause «يعلم ...» has no grammatical position, the ṣila of the implied particle-relative (أن).
The clause «أوتوا ...» has no grammatical position, the ṣila of the relative noun (الذين).
The clause «يؤمنوا ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause يعلم.
The clause «تخبت له قلوبهم» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause يؤمنوا.
The clause «إنّ الله لهادي ...» has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «آمنوا ...» has no grammatical position, the ṣila of the second relative noun (الذين).

* Benefits:
- The saying of Allah the Exalted: أَلْقَى الشَّيْطانُ فِي أُمْنِيَّتِهِ:
"The problem of the Gharānīq (al-gharānīq)": we may not pass over this story the way the noble pass by the banquets of the base, because of its intimate bearing on the essence of the Islamic creed. We shall take up its kernel and leave the husks, in keeping with the plan of the book.
a- The narrator of this legend claimed that the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and his family and grant them peace) wished that nothing of the revelation would descend upon him that would repel Quraysh, hoping for their acceptance of Islam, until Sūrat «al-Najm» was revealed; he began reciting it in the assembly of Quraysh, within their hearing, until he reached His saying «وَمَناةَ الثَّالِثَةَ الْأُخْرى», whereupon Satan cast upon his tongue something answering the wish he had wished, and he said: «تلك الغرانيق العلى، وإن شفاعتهن لترتجى» ("Those are the exalted gharānīq, and their intercession is indeed hoped for"). When he prostrated at its end, everyone in the assembly prostrated with him, and they were pleased. Here are the views of the scholars on this report:
1- al-Rāzī impugned this report, and supported his words with the ḥadīth of al-Bukhārī which mentioned the story of the prostration and did not mention the gharānīq.
2- Ibn al-ʿArabī responds to al-Ṭabarī, and al-Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ supports him; they both say: "This ḥadīth was not transmitted by the people of soundness (ahl al-ṣiḥḥa), nor did a trustworthy narrator relate it with a sound, connected chain, in addition to the weakness of its transmitters, the inconsistency of its versions and the breaks in its chains. Of those Followers (tābiʿūn) and exegetes from whom this story is reported, none of them gave it a chain, nor traced it back to a Companion. Most of the routes from them are weak and flimsy. So this too is a rejected matter.. [Translator's note: the closing quotation mark is missing in the source]
3- It was said: perhaps that was a rebuke to the unbelievers; al-Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ permitted that, on condition that there be a contextual indicator (qarīna) pointing to it.
4- It was said: Quraysh used to make noise and cause confusion over the Messenger's recitation of the Quran, and they tried to mix their speech with the speech of the Messenger (may Allah bless him and his family and grant them peace); this was attributed to Satan because he was behind their tongues.
5- It was said that Satan seized the opportunity of the Messenger's measured recitation (tartīl) of the Quran, and those breaks and pauses he used to make between one verse and another; Satan seized the opportunity of his silence and recited the mentioned words. al-Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ approved this line of interpretation and explanation..
6- al-Qasṭallānī said in the commentary on al-Bukhārī: More than one of the imams has impugned this story. And Ibn Isḥāq said, when asked about it: «It is a fabrication of the zanādiqa (heretics)».
7- al-Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ says: The proof has been established and the Umma has agreed upon his (may Allah bless him and his family and grant them peace) infallibility (ʿiṣma) and his being free of this vice.
8- It has not been heard that any of the polytheists, the hypocrites or the Jews took this story as a weapon with which to oppose Islam and contest the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and his family and grant them peace). So reflect — may Allah protect you from slipping.
9- The Indian scholar Muḥammad ʿAlī rejected the statement of al-Wāqidī and al-Ṭabarī and supported the report of Ibn Isḥāq and al-Bukhārī, the two of which are more worthy of credence and verification, and said: This story has no basis in truth.
10- Imam Muḥammad ʿAbduh says:
This claim of the story is among the ugliest things anyone could imagine regarding Allah the Exalted's singling out of His prophets and His choosing them from the elect of His friends; so let us leave this raving, for it is accepted neither by reason nor by transmitted text — until he says:
Had what the transmitters of the Gharānīq story said been true, trust in the revelation would have been lifted, reliance on it would have been undone, and the greatest pillar of the divine laws, namely infallibility (ʿiṣma), would have collapsed. And the Arabs' describing their gods as "the exalted gharānīq" is not known of them, neither in their poetry nor in their prose.
11- None of the meanings given in the dictionaries for الغرنوق would the Arabs accept as a description of their idols, nor would their eloquent ones accept it. Accordingly, we do not believe that speech to be anything but among the fabrications of the non-Arabs (aʿājim) and the inventions of the obfuscators; it gained currency with those whom a passion for transmission (riwāya) lured away from what understanding (dirāya) requires..
«رَبَّنا لا تُزِغْ قُلُوبَنا بَعْدَ إِذْ هَدَيْتَنا»

safi-cedvel:55-55.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) is resumptive (istiʾnāfiyya); (لا يزال) is an incomplete (nāqiṣ), abrogating (nāsikh) imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ); (في مرية) is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the omitted khabar (predicate) of لا يزال; (منه) is attached to an omitted naʿt (adjective) of (مرية); (حتّى) is a particle of goal (ghāya) and of the genitive; (تأتيهم) is an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by an implied (muḍmara) أن after حتّى; (بغتة) is a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the place of a ḥāl (circumstantial) [Note: Or a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) standing in for the maṣdar, meeting the verb in meaning, i.e. "the Hour comes upon them suddenly (tabghatuhum … baghtatan)".].
The interpreted maṣdar (al-maṣdar al-muʾawwal) (أن تأتيهم) is in the position of the genitive by (حتّى), attached to the "being settled" (al-istiqrār) to which (في مرية) is attached.
The clause «لا يزال الذين ...» has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «كفروا ...» has no grammatical position, the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun (الذين).
The clause «تأتيهم ...» has no grammatical position, the ṣila of the implied (muḍmar) particle-relative (al-mawṣūl al-ḥarfī) (أن).
The clause «يأتيهم عذاب ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause تأتيهم.

* Morphology:
(عقيم): an assimilated adjective (ṣifa mushabbaha) from عقم يعقم, of the bāb of نصر, or the bāb of فرح, or the bāb of كرم; its pattern is فعيل [Note: In the speech there is an implicit metaphor (istiʿāra makniyya), in that the day is likened to a woman who does not give birth; the thing likened to (al-mushabbah bihi) is omitted and replaced by one of its concomitants, by His saying عقيم.].

* Rhetoric:
Metaphor (al-istiʿāra):
In the saying of Allah the Exalted «أَوْ يَأْتِيَهُمْ عَذابُ يَوْمٍ عَقِيمٍ», what is meant is a day of war in which they are killed; it is described as عقيم (barren) because the women's children are killed in it, so they become as though barren, having not given birth; or because fighters are called "sons of war", so when they are killed the day of war is described as barren. On the first view there is a figurative usage in the attribution (majāz fī al-isnād) and a figurative usage in the single word (majāz fī al-mufrad), by making bereavement into barrenness; likewise on the second, because the one who gives birth and the barren one is the war, by way of metaphor by allusion (al-istiʿāra bi-l-kināya), so when the day of war is described by that, it is a figurative usage in the attribution. It was also said: it is the one in which there is no good. One says ريح عقيم (a barren wind) when it does not produce rain nor pollinate trees; on this view there is a subordinate metaphor (istiʿāra tabaʿiyya) in it, because the quality in the day that prevents good is treated as barrenness.

safi-cedvel:56-59.t:
* I'rab:
The tanwīn in (يومئذ) is a compensation (ʿiwaḍ) for an omitted clause, i.e. "the day they believe" or "the day their doubt ceases", and the adverb (ẓarf) is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the "being settled" (al-istiqrār) to which (لله) is attached, i.e. in the khabar (predicate); (بينهم) is an adverb, accusative (manṣūb), attached to (يحكم); (الفاء) is a conjunction for division and consequence (al-taqsīm wa-l-tafrīʿ); (في جنّات) is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (subject) (الذين).
The clause «الملك.. لله) [Translator's note: the closing bracket is so in the source] has no grammatical position, resumptive (istiʾnāfiyya).
The clause «يحكم بينهم» has no grammatical position, an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī) [Note: Or in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the word of majesty (lafẓ al-jalāla), but the governor (ʿāmil) is weak.].
The clause «الذين آمنوا ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause يحكم ...
The clause «آمنوا ...» has no grammatical position, the ṣila (relative clause) of the first relative noun (الذين).
The clause «عملوا ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause آمنوا.
(بآياتنا) is attached to (كذّبوا); (الفاء) in أولئك is redundant (zāʾida) because of the resemblance of the mubtadaʾ to a condition; (أولئك) is a demonstrative in the position of the nominative, a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is the clause لهم عذاب; (لهم) is attached to a fronted khabar of the mubtadaʾ (عذاب).
The clause «الذين كفروا ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause الذين آمنوا.
The clause «كفروا ...» has no grammatical position, the ṣila of the second relative noun (الذين).
The clause «كذّبوا ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause كفروا.
The clause «أولئك لهم عذاب» is in the position of the nominative, the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (الذين كفروا).
The clause «لهم عذاب ...» is in the position of the nominative, the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (أولئك).
(الواو) is a conjunction; (الذين) is a relative noun in the position of the nominative, a mubtadaʾ; (في سبيل) is attached to a ḥāl of the fāʿil (agent) of هاجروا; (قتلوا) is a passive past verb.. and (الواو) is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); (أو) is a conjunction; (اللام) is the lām of the oath, for an implied (muqaddar) oath; (يرزقنّهم) is an imperfect verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa, in the position of the nominative.. and (النون) is the nūn of emphasis, and (هم) is a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi (direct object); (رزقا) is a second mafʿūl bihi, accusative [Note: If it is in the sense of "that which is provided".. and it is a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) if what is intended by it is the bare event.]; (الواو) is resumptive — or parenthetical (iʿtirāḍiyya); (اللام) is the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa), for emphasis ...
The clause «الذين هاجروا ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause الذين كفروا..
The clause «هاجروا ...» has no grammatical position, the ṣila of the third relative noun (الذين).
The clause «قتلوا ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause هاجروا..
The clause «ماتوا ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause قتلوا.
The clause «يرزقنّهم الله ...» has no grammatical position, the response to the implied oath.. and the implied oath clause together with its response is in the position of the nominative, the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (الذين هاجروا).
The clause «إنّ الله لهو ...» has no grammatical position, causal (taʿlīliyya) — or parenthetical between the badal (substitute) and that for which it substitutes (al-mubdal minhu).
The clause «هو خير ...» is in the position of the nominative, the khabar of inna.
(ليدخلنّهم) is like ليرزقنّهم; (مدخلا) is a mafʿūl bihi, accusative [Note: This is if it is a noun of place.. and it is a mafʿūl muṭlaq if it is a mīm-maṣdar (maṣdar mīmī).]; (الواو) is resumptive..
The clause «يدخلنّهم ...» has no grammatical position, the response to an implied oath.. and the clause of the oath and the response has no grammatical position, resumptive.. or a badal of the first oath and its response.
The clause «يرضونه ...» is in the position of the accusative, a naʿt (adjective) of (مدخلا).
The clause «إنّ الله لعليم ...» has no grammatical position, having the status of causation (taʿlīl).

safi-cedvel:60-62.t:
* I'rab:
(ذلك) is a demonstrative in the position of the nominative, the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), its implied form being "the matter" or "the affair"; (الواو) is resumptive (istiʾnāfiyya); (من) is a relative noun, mubtadaʾ [Note: Or it is a conditional noun, a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is the clause عاقب.. and the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted, indicated by the response to the oath لينصرنّه.
(2, 3) In the previous verse (59).] [Translator's note: so in the source; footnotes 2 and 3, both referring to verse 59, have been run into this note]; (بمثل) is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (عاقب); (ما) is a relative noun, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of the genitive, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), and the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) of the passive (عوقب) is a latent (mustatir) pronoun referring back to من; (به) is attached to (عوقب); (عليه) is the nāʾib fāʿil of the passive (بغي); (اللام) is the lām of the oath, for an implied (muqaddar) oath; (ينصرنّ) is an imperfect verb, indeclinable on the fatḥa, in the position of the nominative; (إنّ الله لعفوّ) is like إنّ الله لعليم (2).
The clause «(الأمر) ذلك ...» has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «من عاقب ...» has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «عاقب ...» has no grammatical position, the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun (من).
The clause «عوقب ...» has no grammatical position, the ṣila of the relative noun (ما).
The clause «بغي عليه ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause عاقب.
The clause «ينصرنّه الله ...» has no grammatical position, the response to the implied oath, and the clause of the oath and its response is in the position of the nominative, the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (من) (3); and the clause «إنّ الله لعفوّ ...» has no grammatical position, resumptive.
(ذلك) is a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is (بأنّ الله ...); (في النهار) is attached to (يولج), and likewise (في الليل) to the second (يولج).
The interpreted maṣdar (al-maṣdar al-muʾawwal) (أنّ الله يولج..) is in the position of the genitive by the bāʾ, attached to the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (ذلك).
The interpreted maṣdar (أنّ الله سميع) is in the position of the genitive, conjoined to the first interpreted maṣdar.
The clause «ذلك بأنّ الله ...» has no grammatical position, resumptive and causal (taʿlīliyya).
The clause «يولج الليل ...» is in the position of the nominative, the khabar of the (first) anna.
The clause «يولج النهار ...» is in the position of the nominative, conjoined to the clause يولج الليل.
(ذلك بأنّ الله هو الحقّ) is like ذلك بأنّ الله يولج; (هو) is a detached pronoun, mubtadaʾ, whose khabar is (الحقّ); (الواو) is a conjunction; (ما) is a relative noun in the position of the accusative, the ism of anna; (من دونه) is attached to a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the omitted object; (هو) is a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is (الباطل); (الواو) is a conjunction; (أنّ الله هو العليّ) is like أنّ الله هو الحقّ.
The interpreted maṣdar (أنّ الله هو الحقّ) is in the position of the genitive by the bāʾ, attached to the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (ذلك).
The interpreted maṣdar (أنّ ما يدعون ...) is in the position of the genitive, conjoined to the interpreted maṣdar (أنّ الله هو الحقّ).
The interpreted maṣdar (أنّ الله هو العليّ) is in the position of the genitive, conjoined to the interpreted maṣdar (أنّ الله هو الحقّ).
The clause «ذلك بأنّ الله ...» has no grammatical position, resumptive, reinforcing the causation (taʿlīl).
The clause «هو الحقّ ...» is in the position of the nominative, the khabar of the third (أنّ).
The clause «يدعون ...» has no grammatical position, the ṣila of the relative noun (ما).
The clause «هو الباطل ...» is in the position of the nominative, the khabar of the fourth (أنّ).
The clause «هو العليّ ...» is in the position of the nominative, the khabar of the fifth (أنّ).

safi-cedvel:63-63.t:
* I'rab:
(الهمزة) is interrogative, and it has the meaning of informing (ikhbār); the sign of the jussive (jazm) in (تر) is the deletion of the weak letter; (من السماء) is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (أنزل); (الفاء) is a conjunction [Note: The fāʾ here is not the fāʾ of causation (fāʾ al-sababiyya), because the earth's becoming green is not caused by the seeing; it is caused only by the descent of the rain itself. Moreover, the interrogative means informing and affirmation (taqrīr), i.e. "you have seen that Allah sent down",..].
The interpreted maṣdar (al-maṣdar al-muʾawwal) (أنّ الله أنزل ...) is in the position of the accusative, standing in place of the two objects of ترى.
The clause «لم تر ...» has no grammatical position, resumptive (istiʾnāfiyya).
The clause «أنزل ...» is in the position of the nominative, the khabar (predicate) of anna.
The clause «تصبح الأرض ...» is in the position of the nominative, conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause أنزل [Note: تصبح is in the sense of أصبحت, or it is to indicate the persistence of the rain's effect time after time, as al-Zamakhsharī says..
And the clause, according to Abū al-Baqāʾ, is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), namely the implied pronoun of the story (ḍamīr al-qiṣṣa), and the nominal clause is resumptive.].
The clause «إنّ الله لطيف ...» has no grammatical position, an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī).

* Morphology:
(مخضّرة) [Translator's note: so spelled in the source; the Quranic word is مخضرّة]: feminine of مخضرّ, a passive participle [Translator's note: so in the source; مُخْضَرّ is in fact the active participle of اخضرّ] of the five-letter (khumāsī) اخضرّ; it may be an active participle if we attribute the action of becoming green to the earth itself; its pattern is مفعلّ with ḍamma on the mīm, and the fatḥa did not appear on the first lām because of the doubling (taḍʿīf).

* Rhetoric:
Conjoining a future imperfect to a past verb:
In the saying of Allah the Exalted «أَلَمْ تَرَ أَنَّ اللَّهَ أَنْزَلَ مِنَ السَّماءِ ماءً فَتُصْبِحُ الْأَرْضُ مُخْضَرَّةً», the shift from the past to the imperfect is to convey the persistence of the rain's effect time after time, as you say:
أنعم عليّ فلان عام كذا، فأروح وأغدو شاكرا له (So-and-so bestowed a favour on me in such-and-such a year, so I go out evening and morning grateful to him). Had you said فرحت وغدوت (so I went out evening and morning), it would not have had that effect; or it is to make the wonderful image present (istiḥḍār al-ṣūra).

* Benefits:
1- The saying of Allah the Exalted فَتُصْبِحُ الْأَرْضُ مُخْضَرَّةً: Ibn Hishām said in al-Mughnī:
And it was said: the fāʾ in this verse is for causation, and the fāʾ of causation does not necessitate immediate succession (taʿqīb), as evidenced by our saying: إن يسلم فهو يدخل الجنة (If he becomes Muslim, then he enters Paradise) — do you not see that between the two there is the interval that there is?
2- The signs of His power, exalted is He: al-Rāzī mentioned six things among them:
a- The sending down of water from the sky, and the greening of the earth that arises from it.
b- The comprehensiveness of Allah's dominion, by His saying: له ما في السموات وما في الأرض.
c- The subjecting of everything on earth, plants and animals, to man so that he may benefit from it.
d- The subjecting of ships by the water, and the subjecting of the winds; were it not for these two, man would not be able to move from one place to another with water between them; rather, the ship would stand still with them or sink.
And the holding back of the sky, with the spheres and bodies in it, from falling onto the earth and so taking away all those blessings. [Translator's note: this item is unlabelled in the source, and the next item jumps to "g"]
g- Giving life, then causing death, then giving life again: in the first giving of life are His blessings upon us in this world, and in the second giving of life are His blessings in the Hereafter.

safi-cedvel:64-64.t:
* I'rab:
(له) is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) a fronted khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ (subject) (ما), the relative noun; (في السموات) is attached to an omitted ṣila (relative clause) of ما; (في الأرض) is attached to an omitted ṣila of the second ما; (الواو) is a conjunction; (اللام) is the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa), for emphasis; (الحميد) is a second khabar, nominative (marfūʿ).
The clause «له ما في السموات ...» has no grammatical position, resumptive (istiʾnāfiyya).
The clause «إنّ الله ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the resumptive clause.
The clause «هو الغنيّ ...» is in the position of the nominative, the khabar of inna.

safi-cedvel:65-65.t:
* I'rab:
(ألم تر أنّ الله سخّر) is like ألم تر أنّ الله أنزل [Note: In verse (63) of this sūra.]; (لكم) is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (سخّر); (في الأرض) is attached to an omitted ṣila (relative clause) of ما; (الواو) is a conjunction; (الفلك) is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to (ما), accusative (manṣūb) [Note: It may be conjoined to the word of majesty (lafẓ al-jalāla), and the clause تجري is then a khabar (predicate).]; (في البحر) is attached to (تجري); (بأمره) is attached to a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the fāʿil (agent) of تجري, i.e. "accompanied" or "made to sail".
The interpreted maṣdar (al-maṣdar al-muʾawwal) (أنّ الله سخّر ...) is in the position of the accusative, standing in place of the two objects of ترى.
The interpreted maṣdar (أن تقع ...) is in the position of the accusative, a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose) with a muḍāf omitted, i.e. "for fear of its falling" [Note: The interpreted maṣdar may be accusative as a badal (substitute) of السماء, a badal of inclusion (badal ishtimāl), i.e. "He holds back the falling of the sky", i.e. He prevents its falling.].
(على الأرض) is attached to (تقع); (إلّا) is a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr) [Note: Or a particle of exception, for an emptied exception (istithnāʾ mufarragh).], and the negation before it is implied by the verb يمسك, i.e. "He does not leave"; (بإذنه) is attached to a ḥāl, and (الباء) is for accompaniment (mulābasa) [Note: I.e. it is excepted from the generality of states.. i.e. He holds back the sky from falling in every state except in the state of His permission.]; (بالناس) is attached to (رؤف); (رحيم) is a second khabar of (إنّ).
The clause «لم تر ...» has no grammatical position, resumptive (istiʾnāfiyya).
The clause «سخّر ...» is in the position of the nominative, the khabar of anna.
The clause «تجري ...» is in the position of the accusative, a ḥāl of الفلك [Note: Or it is conjoined to the clause سخّر — so it is in meaning a khabar — if (الفلك) is conjoined to the word of majesty الله.].
The clause «يمسك ...» has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «تقع ...» has no grammatical position, the ṣila of the particle-relative (al-mawṣūl al-ḥarfī) (أن).
The clause «إنّ الله.. لرؤوف ...» has no grammatical position, an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī).

* Morphology:
(تقع): it contains iʿlāl (weak-letter change) by deletion, for it is the imperfect of the mithāl (first-radical weak) verb وقع, of the bāb of فتح; its pattern is تعل with two fatḥas.

safi-cedvel:66-66.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) is resumptive (istiʾnāfiyya); (الذي) is the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ (subject) هو; (ثمّ) is a conjunction in both places; (اللام) is the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa), for emphasis. The clause «هو الذي ...» has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «أحياكم ...» has no grammatical position, the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun (الذي).
The clause «يميتكم ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the ṣila clause.
The clause «يحييكم ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause يميتكم.
The clause «إنّ الإنسان لكفور» has no grammatical position, resumptive.

safi-cedvel:67-69.t:
* I'rab:
(لكلّ) is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted second mafʿūl bihi (direct object) whose governor (ʿāmil) is جعلنا; (الفاء) links (rābiṭa) the apodosis of an implied condition; (لا) is prohibitive, making jussive (nāhiya jāzima); (ينازعنّك) is an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm), the sign of its jussive being the deletion of the nūn, for it is one of the five verbs (al-afʿāl al-khamsa) ... and (الواو), deleted because of the meeting of two quiescent letters, is the fāʿil (agent), and (النون) is the nūn of emphasis; (في الأمر) is attached to (ينازعنّك); (الواو) is a conjunction; (إلى ربّك) is attached to (ادع) with a muḍāf omitted, i.e. "to the religion of your Lord"; (اللام) is the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa), for emphasis; (على هدى) is attached to the khabar (predicate) of inna; (مستقيم) is a naʿt (adjective) of هدى, genitive (majrūr).
The clause «جعلنا ...» has no grammatical position, resumptive (istiʾnāfiyya).
The clause «هم ناسكوه ...» is in the position of the accusative, a naʿt of (منسكا).
The clause «لا ينازعنّك ...» is in the position of the jussive, the apodosis of an implied condition.. i.e. "if they dispute with you about the matter of the sacred law, then let them not contend with you" — i.e. do not contend with them — and the clause «ادع ...» is in the position of the jussive, conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause لا ينازعنّك.
The clause «إنّك لعلى هدى ...» has no grammatical position, causal (taʿlīliyya).
(الواو) is a conjunction; (جادلوك) is a past verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the ḍamma, in the position of the jussive as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ). And (الواو) is the fāʿil, and (الكاف) is a mafʿūl bihi; (الفاء) links the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); (ما) is a maṣdar-forming particle (ḥarf maṣdarī) [Note: Or a relative noun, with the referent pronoun (ʿāʾid) omitted, i.e. تعملونه.].
The interpreted maṣdar (al-maṣdar al-muʾawwal) (ما تعملون) is in the position of the genitive by the bāʾ, attached to (أعلم), i.e. "knowing" (ʿālim). And the clause «إن جادلوك ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the implied conditional clause ناقشوك.
The clause «قل ...» is in the position of the jussive, the apodosis, joined with the fāʾ.
The clause «الله أعلم ...» is in the position of the accusative, the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl).
The clause «تعملون ...» has no grammatical position, the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative (ما), the particle or the noun.
(بينكم) is an adverb (ẓarf), accusative (manṣūb), attached to (يحكم), and likewise (يوم); (ما) is a relative noun in the position of the genitive by the preposition, attached to (يحكم); (فيه) is attached to (تختلفون).
The clause «الله يحكم ...» has no grammatical position, an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī).
The clause «يحكم بينكم ...» is in the position of the nominative, the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (subject) (الله).
The clause «كنتم فيه تختلفون ...» has no grammatical position, the ṣila of the relative noun (ما).
The clause «تختلفون» is in the position of the accusative, the khabar of كنتم.

* Morphology:
(ناسكوه): plural of ناسك, the active participle of the triliteral نسك; its pattern is فاعل, and the nūn of the plural has been deleted because of the iḍāfa (annexation).

* Benefits:
- وَإِنْ جادَلُوكَ فَقُلِ اللَّهُ أَعْلَمُ بِما تَعْمَلُونَ «Disputation (al-jadal) in Islam»:
Many are the verses that deal with disputation, once under this name, and once as argumentation (al-ḥijāj); in general Allah calls us to dispute in the way that is best. And at times He calls us to turn away from the ignorant.
The imams of the schools differed about disputation and argumentation.
a- Mālik used to detest disputation and debate (munāẓara), and held that knowledge is أزمع [Translator's note: so in the source; probably a misprint for أرفع, "loftier"] than to be taken as a path to assault and contest.. He once said to the caliph al-Rashīd, when the latter asked him to debate one of the jurists — he asked the Commander of the Faithful to excuse him from that, saying: It is not permissible for us to treat knowledge like the setting of cocks against each other.. or the stirring up of dogs.
b- Imam al-Shāfiʿī used to debate for the sake of bringing the truth to light, and he used to say: I never debated anyone without wishing that Allah would make the truth appear on his tongue. He was calm, gentle and deliberate in his debates, and sincere in his disputations.
c- Imam Abū Ḥanīfa opened the door of debate wide, until his school became the school of the people of opinion (aṣḥāb al-raʾy).
d- Imam Aḥmad ibn Ḥanbal never permitted himself to enter the door of disputation at all; and each of them had his reasons and motives — may Allah be pleased with them all.

safi-cedvel:70-70.t:
* I'rab:
(ألم تعلم أن الله يعلم) is like ألم تر أن الله أنزل [Note: In verse (63) of this sūra.]; (ما) is a relative noun, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of the accusative, a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); (في السموات) is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted ṣila (relative clause) of ما; the demonstrative (ذلك) refers to what exists in the heaven and the earth; (في كتاب) is attached to the khabar (predicate) of inna; the second demonstrative (ذلك) refers to Allah's knowledge; (على الله) is attached to (يسير).
The clause «تعلم ...» has no grammatical position, resumptive (istiʾnāfiyya).
The clause «يعلم ...» is in the position of the nominative, the khabar of anna.
The interpreted maṣdar (al-maṣdar al-muʾawwal) (أنّ الله يعلم ...» is in the position of the accusative, standing in place of the two objects of تعلم.
The clause «أنّ ذلك في كتاب» [Translator's note: so in the source, with أنّ; the verse has إنّ] has no grammatical position, causal (taʿlīliyya).
The clause «إنّ ذلك.. يسير» has no grammatical position, an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī).

safi-cedvel:71-72.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) is resumptive (istiʾnāfiyya); (من دون) is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the relative noun ما, and the fāʿil (agent) of (ينزّل) is a pronoun referring to the word of majesty (lafẓ al-jalāla); (به) is attached to (ينزّل) [Note: Or to an omitted ḥāl of (سلطانا) — a naʿt (adjective) placed before what it qualifies.]; the second (ما) is a relative noun conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the first ما, in the position of the accusative; (لهم) is attached to the khabar (predicate) of ليس; (به) is attached to a ḥāl of (علم), which is the ism of ليس; (الواو) is circumstantial (ḥāliyya) — or resumptive; (للظالمين) is attached to a fronted khabar; (نصير) is genitive (majrūr) in form and nominative in position, a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject).
The clause «يعبدون ...» has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «لم ينزّل ...» has no grammatical position, the ṣila (relative clause) of the first relative noun (ما).
The clause «ليس لهم به علم» has no grammatical position, the ṣila of the second relative noun (ما).
The clause «ما للظالمين من نصير» is in the position of the accusative, a ḥāl [Note: Or resumptive, with no grammatical position.].
(الواو) is a conjunction; (عليهم) is attached to the passive verb (تتلى); (بيّنات) is a ḥāl of the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) آياتنا; (في وجوه) is attached to (تعرف); (بالذين) is attached to (يسطون) by its being made to include (taḍmīn) the meaning of يبطشون ("they seize violently"); (عليهم) is attached to (يتلون); (الهمزة) is interrogative; (الفاء) is a conjunction; (بشّر) is attached to (أنبّئكم); (من ذلكم) is attached to (شرّ); (النار) is a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is the clause وعدها [Note: Or it is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, its implied form being هو.. and the clause is an explanatory resumption, and the clause وعدها is a second khabar of the mubtadaʾ هو.], and (الهاء) in (وعدها) is the second object; (الذين) is the first object [Note: The relative noun may properly be the second object if the Fire is the devourer and the unbelievers are devoured.]; (الواو) is resumptive; (بئس) is an inflexible (jāmid) past verb for expressing blame (inshāʾ al-dhamm), and the one specified for blame (al-makhṣūṣ bi-l-dhamm) is omitted, its implied form being هي, i.e. the Fire.
The clause «تتلى ... آياتنا» is in the position of the genitive, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct).
The clause «تعرف ...» has no grammatical position, the apodosis of a non-jussive condition (jawāb sharṭ ghayr jāzim).
The clause «كفروا ...» has no grammatical position, the ṣila of the relative noun (الذين).
The clause «يكادون ...» is in the position of the accusative, a ḥāl of the relative noun [Note: The muḍāf is part of the muḍāf ilayhi.. and it may be a ḥāl of وجوه, since they are its owners (aṣḥābuhā).].
The clause «يسطون ...» is in the position of the accusative, the khabar of يكادون.
The clause «يتلون ...» has no grammatical position, the ṣila of the second relative noun (الذين).
The clause «قل ...» has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «أفأنبّئكم ...» is in the position of the accusative, conjoined to an implied clause which is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl), i.e. "Shall I address you, and so inform you".
The clause «النار وعدها ...» has no grammatical position, explaining الشرّ.. or an explanatory resumption.
The clause «وعدها ...» is in the position of the nominative, the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (النار).
The clause «كفروا ...» has no grammatical position, the ṣila of the third relative noun (الذين).
The clause «بئس المصير ...» has no grammatical position, resumptive.

* Morphology:
(يسطون), in the sense of "they overpower" or "they subdue": it contains iʿlāl (weak-letter change) by deletion; its origin is يسطوون — with two wāws; two quiescent letters met, so the weak letter, the lām of the word, was deleted and it became يسطون; its pattern is يفعون.

safi-cedvel:73-74.t:
* I'rab:
(أيّ) is the one addressed (munādā), an intended indefinite (nakira maqṣūda), indeclinable (mabnī) on the ḍamma, in the position of the accusative.. and (ها) is a particle for drawing attention (tanbīh); (الناس) is a badal (substitute) of أيّ — or an ʿaṭf bayān (explicative apposition) — following it in the nominative in form (lafẓan); (الفاء) links (rābiṭa) the effect to the cause; (له) is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (استمعوا); (من دون) is attached to a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the omitted referent pronoun (ʿāʾid), i.e. "whom you worship, being other than Allah"; (الواو) is circumstantial (ḥāliyya); (لو) is a non-jussive conditional particle; (له) is attached to (اجتمعوا); (الواو) is a conjunction; (شيئا) is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (manṣūb); (يستنقذوه) is an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) as the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), the sign of its jussive being the deletion of the nūn; (منه) is attached to (يستنقذوه).
The clause «the vocative: يا أيّها الناس ...» has no grammatical position, resumptive (istiʾnāfiyya).
The clause «ضرب مثل ...» has no grammatical position, the response to the vocative.
The clause «استمعوا ...» is in the position of the jussive, the apodosis of an implied condition, i.e.: "if you want the lesson, then listen".
The clause «إنّ الذين تدعون ...» has no grammatical position, an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī).
The clause «تدعون من دون الله ...» has no grammatical position, the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun (الذين).
The clause «لن يخلقوا ...» is in the position of the nominative, the khabar (predicate) of inna.
The clause «اجتمعوا ...» is in the position of the accusative, a ḥāl.. and the apodosis of (لو) is omitted, explained by what is mentioned before it, i.e.: "they will not create a fly".
The clause «إن يسلبهم الذباب ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause إنّ الذين تدعون.
The clause «لا يستنقذوه ...» has no grammatical position, the apodosis not joined with the fāʾ.
The clause «ضعف الطالب ...» has no grammatical position, an explanatory resumption — or an affirming one (taqrīrī). (ما) is negating; (حقّ) is a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) standing in for the maṣdar (verbal noun), for it is annexed to the maṣdar, accusative; (اللام) is the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa), for emphasis.
The clause «ما قدروا ...» has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «إنّ الله لقويّ ...» has no grammatical position, causal (taʿlīliyya).

* Morphology:
(ذبابا): a generic noun (ism jins) whose singular is ذبابة, on the measure فعالة; it is pluralised as ذبّان, with kasra or ḍamma on the dhāl and doubling of the bāʾ, and as أذبّة, on the measure أغربة; it is taken from ذبّ when it means "drove away" and آب when it means "returned".
(الطالب): active participle of the triliteral طلب; its pattern is فاعل.
(المطلوب): passive participle of the triliteral طلب; its pattern is مفعول.

* Benefits:
1- The parable (al-mathal) in the Quran:
We have pointed out repeatedly the role of the parable in the Noble Quran. We return here to pause at this verse, which compares the power of the alleged gods — whether human, animal or inanimate — and their inability to create a single fly, even if they backed one another up, with the power of the fly, which is among the weakest of Allah's creation, yet it may assault what is in the possession of man and of all those gods, and rob them of some of it, and that which is robbed stands helpless before the fly, unable to rescue what was taken from it.
Is it not right that we describe both the robber and the robbed as weak?! Perhaps this verse inspired that Western philosopher to say: Science has failed to this day to uncover the reality of a fly.. He drew his faith in the able Power that has dominion over this existence from the precision of Allah's creatures, and from the inability of man and his science to grasp the secret of life in the weakest of the living among Allah's creatures. How splendid is the saying of Allah the Exalted at the close of this verse «ضَعُفَ الطَّالِبُ وَالْمَطْلُوبُ. ما قَدَرُوا اللَّهَ حَقَّ قَدْرِهِ». Thus we find that the parable on one side, dialogue on a second, the story on a third, and personified images full of life and movement — all are among the elements making up the style of the Noble Quran, its eloquence and its inimitability (iʿjāz).
2- Novelty in the invention of meanings (jiddat ikhtirāʿ al-maʿānī):
It is that the poet or writer invents a meaning in which he has had no predecessor. His saying, exalted is He, «إِنَّ الَّذِينَ تَدْعُونَ مِنْ دُونِ اللَّهِ لَنْ يَخْلُقُوا ذُباباً» is among the most eloquent things Allah has revealed in showing up the ignorance of the unbelievers, rebuking them and belittling their intellects, because of the strangeness of the comparison, which contains extreme hyperbole while remaining bound to truth and reality.
For He, glorified is He, restricted Himself to mentioning the weakest of creatures and the least of them in robbing what it robs, and to declaring everyone besides Him incapable of creating its like, even with mutual support and gathering together; then He turned from the level of creating, because of the incapacitation in it, to the rescuing of the meagre little that the fly robs; thus He descended by degrees, as the plan of eloquence requires in ordering.
Novelty of invention in meanings, among poets and men of letters, is a charming and extremely useful subject. Were it not for fear of departing from our plan of brevity, we would have presented to you handfuls of the choicest inventions of Abū Tammām, al-Mutanabbī, Ibn al-Rūmī, al-Jāḥiẓ and many others besides; so if you are one of the knights of this field, then turn to the dīwāns of these men.

safi-cedvel:75-76.t:
* I'rab:
(من الملائكة) is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (يصطفي), and likewise (من الناس); (بصير) is a second khabar (predicate), nominative (marfūʿ). The clause «الله يصطفى ...» has no grammatical position, resumptive (istiʾnāfiyya).
The clause «يصطفي ...» is in the position of the nominative, the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (subject) (الله).
The clause «إنّ الله سميع ...» has no grammatical position, an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī) — or an affirming one (taqrīrī). (ما) is a relative noun, mafʿūl bihi (direct object), in the position of the accusative; (بين) is an adverb (ẓarf), accusative (manṣūb), attached to an omitted ṣila (relative clause) of ما; (ما خلفهم) is like ما بين.. and conjoined (maʿṭūf) to it; (الواو) is a conjunction; (إلى الله) is attached to the passive verb (ترجع)..
The clause «يعلم ...» has no grammatical position, resumptive [Note: Or in the position of the nominative, a third khabar of the particle resembling the verb (al-ḥarf al-mushabbah bi-l-fiʿl) إنّ..].
The clause «ترجع الأمور» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause يعلم.

* Morphology:
(يصطفي): it contains the substitution (ibdāl) of the tāʾ of the iftiʿāl form into ṭāʾ, because it comes after the ṣād; its origin is يصتفي.

safi-cedvel:77-78.t:
* I'rab:
(يا أيّها الذين آمنوا) is like يا أيّها الناس [Note: In verse (73) of this sūra.]; (الواو) is a conjunction in the three places..
The clause «يأيّها الذين ...» has no grammatical position, resumptive (istiʾnāfiyya).
The clause «آمنوا ...» has no grammatical position, the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun (الذين).
The clause «اركعوا ...» has no grammatical position, the response to the vocative.
The clause «اسجدوا ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the response to the vocative.
The clause «اعبدوا ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the response to the vocative.
The clause «لعلّكم تفلحون» has no grammatical position, an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī), and the clause «تفلحون» is in the position of the nominative, the khabar (predicate) of لعلّكم.
(الواو) is a conjunction; (في الله) is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (جاهدوا) with two muḍāfs omitted, i.e. "in establishing the religion of Allah"; (حق جهاده) is like حقّ قدره [Note: In verse (74) of this sūra.]; (الواو) is a conjunction; (ما) is negating; (عليكم) is attached to an omitted second mafʿūl bihi (direct object) whose governor (ʿāmil) is جعل; (في الدين) is attached to (جعل) [Note: Or attached to a ḥāl (circumstantial) of حرج, or to a ḥāl of the pronoun in (عليكم).]; (حرج) is genitive (majrūr) in form and accusative in position, a first mafʿūl bihi whose governor is جعل; (ملّة) is a mafʿūl bihi of an omitted verb, its implied form being اتّبعوا [Note: Or it is accusative by the import of what precedes it, with a muḍāf omitted, as though He said: "He made your religion broad, as the broadness of the religion of your father", so it is a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) of an omitted verb ... al-Suyūṭī followed al-Farrāʾ in making it accusative by removal of the preposition (manṣūb bi-nazʿ al-khāfiḍ), namely the kāf, and Abū al-Baqāʾ made it a ḥāl with a muḍāf omitted, i.e. "like the religion of your father".], and the sign of the genitive in (أبيكم) is the yāʾ; (إبراهيم) is an ʿaṭf bayān (explicative apposition) of أبيكم, genitive, the sign of its genitive being the fatḥa; (المسلمين) is a second mafʿūl bihi whose governor is سمّاكم, the sign of its accusative being the yāʾ; (قبل) is an adverbial noun, indeclinable (mabnī) on the ḍamma, in the position of the genitive by the preposition, attached to (سمّاكم) [Note: It is made indeclinable on the ḍamma because it is cut off from annexation in wording, i.e. "before this Book"..]; (في هذا) is attached to (سمّاكم), and the demonstrative refers to the Quran; (اللام) is the lām of causation (taʿlīl); (يكون) is an incomplete (nāqiṣ), abrogating (nāsikh) imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by an implied (muḍmara) أن after the lām; (عليكم) is attached to (شهيدا); (تكونوا) is conjoined to يكون, accusative, the sign of its accusative being the deletion of the nūn; (على الناس) is attached to (شهداء); (الفاء) links (rābiṭa) the apodosis of an implied condition; (بالله) is attached to (اعتصموا); (الفاء) is resumptive, and the one specified for praise (al-makhṣūṣ bi-l-madḥ) of the two verbs of praise is omitted, its implied form being هو, i.e. Allah.
The clause «جاهدوا ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the response to the vocative.
The clause «هو اجتباكم ...» has no grammatical position, causal (taʿlīliyya).
The clause «اجتباكم ...» is in the position of the nominative, the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (subject) (هو).
The clause «ما جعل ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause هو اجتباكم [Note: It may be resumptive, and so also have no grammatical position.].
The clause «(اتّبعوا) ملّة أبيكم ...» has no grammatical position, an explanatory resumption [Note: Among the possible cases of the accusative of (ملّة) is its being accusative by an omitted verb, its implied form being أعني ("I mean"), as though there were an implied question after the saying of Allah the Exalted: ما جعل عليكم في الدين من حرج.. "Which religion is it?", and the answer: "I mean the religion of your father".. so on this view the clause is an explanatory resumption.].
The clause «هو سمّاكم ...» has no grammatical position, causal.
The clause «سمّاكم ...» is in the position of the nominative, the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (هو).
The clause «يكون الرسول ...» has no grammatical position, the ṣila of the implied (muḍmar) particle-relative (al-mawṣūl al-ḥarfī) (أن).
The interpreted maṣdar (al-maṣdar al-muʾawwal) (أن يكون ...) is in the position of the genitive by the lām, attached to (سمّاكم).
The clause «تكونوا ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the ṣila of the particle-relative.
The clause «أقيموا ...» is in the position of the jussive (majzūm), the apodosis of an implied condition, i.e.: "if you are worthy of this name, then establish ..."
The clause «آتوا ...» is in the position of the jussive, conjoined to the clause أقيموا.
The clause «اعتصموا ...» is in the position of the jussive, conjoined to the clause أقيموا.
The clause «هو مولاكم ...» is in the position of the accusative, a ḥāl of the word of majesty (lafẓ al-jalāla).
The clause «نعم المولى ...» has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «نعم النصير ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause نعم المولى..

* Morphology:
(جهاد): an aurally-transmitted (samāʿī) maṣdar (verbal noun) of the quadriliteral verb جاهد; its pattern is فعال with kasra on the fāʾ; as for the regular (qiyāsī) maṣdar, it is مجاهدة, its pattern مفاعلة with fatḥa on the fāʾ and fatḥa on the ʿayn.
(سمّاكم): it contains iʿlāl (weak-letter change) by conversion (qalb); its origin is سمّيكم; the yāʾ was voweled after a fatḥa, so it was converted into an alif; its pattern is فعّلكم.

* Benefits:
- وَما جَعَلَ عَلَيْكُمْ فِي الدِّينِ مِنْ حَرَجٍ.
The removal of hardship (rafʿ al-ḥaraj) in Islam:
Some of the mujtahid imams took this heading as one of the principles of jurisprudence (uṣūl al-fiqh) in Islam, and in this decision of theirs they relied on many texts established in the Noble Quran, such as the saying of Allah the Exalted:
«إِنَّ مَعَ الْعُسْرِ يُسْراً». And this verse we are dealing with: «وَما جَعَلَ عَلَيْكُمْ فِي الدِّينِ مِنْ حَرَجٍ». And the saying of Allah the Exalted «لا يُكَلِّفُ اللَّهُ نَفْساً إِلَّا وُسْعَها», and His saying «رَبَّنا وَلا تُحَمِّلْنا ما لا طاقَةَ لَنا بِهِ». And the shortening of the prayer while travelling, and the permission to break the fast in Ramaḍān for whoever is ill or on a journey, etc. And in the noble ḥadīth,
his saying (may Allah bless him and his family and grant them peace): «ما خيّرت بين أمرين إلا اخترت أيسرهما» ("I was never given a choice between two matters but that I chose the easier of them")
and his saying «يسروا ولا تعسروا. إلخ» ("Make things easy and do not make them difficult", etc.)
and his forbidding his Companions to be severe with one another in religion,
and his saying, may Allah bless him and his family and grant them peace: (أما والله إني لأخشاكم لله، وأتقاكم له لكني: أصوم، وأفطر، وأصلي، وأرقد، وأتزوج النساء، فمن رغب عن سنتي مني) ("By Allah, I am the one of you who most fears Allah and is most mindful of Him, but I fast and break my fast, I pray and I sleep, and I marry women; so whoever turns away from my Sunna, [is not] of me") [Translator's note: the word فليس, "is not", is missing in the source text of the ḥadīth].
And much the like of that we find in the books of the Sīra and the Ṣaḥīḥ collections.
المجتهدين [Translator's note: the beginning of this sentence appears to be missing in the source; it reads literally: "… of the mujtahids, the gist of which is"] «It is easy for anyone to be as strict in religion as he wishes, and to issue restrictive rulings upon the Muslims, and there is no great benefit in that. But what is required — and what only one of superior ability and sound mind can undertake — is making things easy for the Muslims, finding ways out of predicaments, and effective solutions for emergent affairs and newly arising problems.. [Translator's note: the closing quotation mark is missing in the source]

safi-cedvel:1-2.t:
* I'rab:
(أيّ) is a vocative, indefinite but specified (nakira maqṣūda), indeclinable (mabnī) on ḍamma, in the position of accusative..
(ها) is a particle of alert; (الناس) is a badal (substitute) for أيّ or an ʿaṭf bayān (explicative apposition), nominative in form.
The vocative clause «يأيّها ... » has no grammatical position; it is an opening clause.
The clause «اتّقوا ... » has no grammatical position; it is the response to the vocative.
The clause «إنّ زلزلة.. شيء» has no grammatical position; it is causal, or an explanatory resumption. (يوم) is an adverb of time, accusative, attached to (تذهل) «[Note: or it is attached to عظيم, or it is a badal ishtimāl (inclusive substitute) for زلزلة الساعة, in which case the clause تذهل is a ḥāl from the hāʾ in ترونها.. It may also be a direct object of an omitted verb, its implied form being "udhkur" (remember).]», (عمّا) is attached to (تذهل) «[Note: (ما) is either a maṣdar particle, the interpreted maṣdar being in the position of genitive, or a relative noun with the returning pronoun omitted.]», (سكارى) is a ḥāl, accusative, from الناس, the sign of the accusative being an implied fatḥa on the alif; (الواو) is circumstantial (ḥāliyya); (ما) is negative, operating like laysa; the second (سكارى) is genitive in form, accusative in position, the khabar of mā; (الواو) is a conjunction; (لكنّ) is a particle resembling the verb, for rectification (istidrāk), an operator (nāsikh). The clause «ترونها ... » is in the position of genitive as the second term of a construct.
The clause «تذهل كلّ ... » has no grammatical position; it is an explanatory resumption «[Note: They allowed the clause to be a ḥāl from الزلزلة or from الساعة, because the first term of the construct is part of the second term, and it has the sense of the agent or the object of الزلزلة.. in which case a pronoun is implied in the clause, i.e. "in it"..]».
The clause «أرضعت ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the particle-maṣdar or the relative noun (ما).
The clause «تضع كلّ ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause تذهل كلّ ...
The clause «ترى ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause تذهل كلّ.
The clause «ما هم بسكارى ... » is in the position of accusative, a ḥāl from الناس.
The clause «لكنّ عذاب.. شديد» has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to an implied resumption, i.e. "all this is easy, but the punishment of Allah is severe".

* Morphology:
(زلزلة) is the regular maṣdar of the quadriliteral verb زلزل, on the wazn فعللة; there is another maṣdar, زلزال, on the wazn فِعلال with kasra on the fāʾ.
(مرضعة) is the active participle of the quadriliteral verb أرضع, on the wazn مُفعِلة with ḍamma on the mīm and kasra on the ʿayn. The tāʾ is attached to it to indicate one who is actually engaged in nursing; without the tāʾ, it is for one whose nature it is to nurse, even if she is not doing so.

* Rhetoric:
Eloquent simile (al-tashbīh al-balīgh):
In the words of the Exalted وَتَرَى النَّاسَ سُكارى وَما هُمْ بِسُكارى. The people on that terrible day are likened to the state of drunkards who have lost discernment and squandered right judgement. The scholars say: one of the proofs of figurative usage is that its opposite can also be truthfully said, as when you say "Zayd is a donkey", describing him as dull and stupid, and then it is true to say "he is not a donkey", denying the literal sense. So it is with the verse: after affirming figurative drunkenness, it denied the literal in the most emphatic denial, strengthened by the bāʾ. The secret of its emphasis is to alert that this drunkenness which afflicts them in that state is nothing of the familiar kind, but something they had never known the like of before. The rectification in the words «وَلكِنَّ عَذابَ اللَّهِ شَدِيدٌ» refers back to His words وما هم بسكارى من الخمر ("they are not drunk from wine"), which is the familiar drunkenness. So what is this strange drunkenness, and what is its cause? It was said: the severity of the punishment of Allah the Exalted.

* Benefits:
- وتضع كل ذات حمل حملها.
«ذات» is a demonstrative for the feminine singular.
The demonstrative is one of the six definite nouns (maʿārif).
The demonstratives are as follows:
a- ذا for the masculine singular.
b- ذي, تي, ذه, ته, ذه, ته, ذا, تا, ذه, ته with the kasra lengthened in both. Thus they become ten for the feminine singular.
c- ذان for the masculine dual in the nominative, تان for the feminine dual in the nominative, and «ذين and تين» for the masculine and feminine dual in the accusative and genitive.
d- «أولاء» for the plural of rational beings, masculine and feminine; it may rarely come for the non-rational, as in the verse of Jarīr:
ذمّ المنازل بعد منزلة اللوى ... والعيش بعد أولئك الأيام
(Censure the abodes after the abode at al-Liwā, and life after those days.)
e- The «kāf of address» and the «lām of distance» are attached to the demonstrative.
A near place is indicated by «هنا» without «ها», or «هاهنا» joined with «ها». A far place is indicated by «هناك or ها هناك or هنالك or هنّا or هينا or هنّت or ثمّ», as in «وَأَزْلَفْنا ثَمَّ الْآخَرِينَ».
Note: if ذات is annexed to adverbs, it is an adverb..

safi-cedvel:3-4.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) is resumptive; (من الناس) is attached to an omitted fronted khabar; (من) is a relative noun, indeclinable, in the position of nominative as a postponed mubtadaʾ; (في الله) is attached to (يجادل) with an omitted muḍāf, i.e. "concerning the power of Allah"; (بغير) is attached to a ḥāl from the agent of يجادل, i.e.:
"enveloped in ignorance".
The clause «من الناس من يجادل ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
The clause «يجادل ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the relative noun (من).
The clause «يتّبع ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause يجادل.
(عليه) is attached to the passive verb كتب, which has been made to include the sense of "was decreed"; the third-person pronoun refers to the devil.. and the (هاء) in (أنّه) is the pronoun of the matter (ḍamīr al-shaʾn), the ism of anna; (من) is a conditional noun that jusses, indeclinable, in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ; (الفاء) links the apodosis; (إلى عذاب) is attached to (يهديه).
The interpreted maṣdar (أنّه من تولّاه..) is in the position of nominative, nāʾib fāʿil of the verb كتب ...
The interpreted maṣdar (أنّه يضلّه..) is in the position of nominative, a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is omitted, i.e. "so his misleading him is bound to occur or take place" «[Note: the interpreted maṣdar may be the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, the implied form being: the way of the devil is to mislead whoever takes him as ally.]».
The clause «كتب عليه ... » is in the position of genitive, an adjective of شيطان «[Note: it may be resumptive, with no grammatical position.]».
The clause «من تولّاه ... » is in the position of nominative, khabar of the (first) anna.
The clause «تولّاه ... » is in the position of nominative, khabar of the mubtadaʾ (من).
The clause «يضلّه ... » is in the position of nominative, khabar of the second (أنّ).
The clause «إضلاله (حاصل)» is in the position of jussive, apodosis of the condition, joined with the fāʾ.
The clause «يهديه» is in the position of nominative, conjoined to the clause يضلّه.

safi-cedvel:5-5.t:
* I'rab:
(يأيّها الناس) its i'rab has been given earlier «[Note: in verse (1) of this surah.]», (كنتم) is a defective (nāqiṣ) past verb, an operator (nāsikh), indeclinable on sukūn, in the position of jussive, the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); (في ريب) is attached to an omitted khabar of كنتم; (من البعث) is attached to (ريب), or to an adjective of (ريب); (الفاء) links the apodosis; (من تراب) is attached to (خلقناكم) with an omitted muḍāf, i.e.: "your father", and conjoined to it with the conjunctions (ثمّ), from His words (من نطفة) up to His words (من مضغة); (غير) is conjoined to مخلّقة, genitive; (اللام) is for causation; (نبيّن) is an imperfect verb, accusative through an implied an after the lām.. the agent is "we", expressing grandeur, and its object is omitted, i.e. "the perfection of our power"; (لكم) is attached to (نبيّن); (الواو) is resumptive; (في الأرحام) is attached to (نقرّ); (إلى أجل) is attached to (نقرّ)..
The interpreted maṣdar (أن نبيّن) is in the position of genitive, attached to (خلقناكم).
(طفلا) is an accusative ḥāl from the object of نخرجكم «[Note: الطفل is put in the singular either because it is originally a maṣdar, or because the genus is intended, or because the meaning is "We bring out each one of you".]», (اللام) is the lām of consequence (ṣayrūra); (تبلغوا) is an imperfect verb, accusative through an implied an after the lām, the sign of the accusative being the dropping of the nūn.. and (الواو) is the agent.
The interpreted maṣdar (أن تبلغوا..) is in the position of genitive through the lām, attached to an omitted verb conjoined to نخرجكم by the conjunction (ثمّ), i.e.: "then We grant you long life so that you reach ...".
(الواو) is a conjunction; (منكم) is attached to an omitted fronted khabar; (من) is a relative noun, indeclinable, in the position of nominative as a postponed mubtadaʾ, and the nāʾib fāʿil of the passive verb (يتوفّى) is a pronoun referring to من, which is the returning pronoun (ʿāʾid); (الواو) is a conjunction; (منكم من يردّ) is like منكم من يتوفّى; (إلى أرذل) is attached to (يردّ); (لكيلا) consists of a preposition, a maṣdar and accusative particle, and a negative particle; (من بعد) is attached to (يعلم).
The interpreted maṣdar (كيلا يعلم..) is in the position of genitive through the lām, attached to (يردّ).
(الواو) is a conjunction; (ترى) is an imperfect verb, nominative, the seeing being visual, and the agent is "you"; (هامدة) is an accusative ḥāl; (الفاء) is a conjunction; (عليها) is attached to (أنزلنا); (ربت) is a past verb, indeclinable on an implied fatḥa on the omitted alif (dropped because of the meeting of two quiescent letters), and the agent is "she"; (من كلّ) is attached to (أنبتت), and its object is omitted, i.e. "things" or "kinds"..
The clause «يأيّها الناس ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
The clause «إن كنتم ... » has no grammatical position; it is the response to the vocative.
The clause «إنّا خلقناكم ... » has no grammatical position; it is a justification for the omitted apodosis, i.e. "if you are in doubt.. then look at what is around you, for We created you" «[Note: the clause إنّا خلقناكم.. may be in the position of jussive, apodosis of the condition, joined with the fāʾ.]».
The clause «خلقناكم ... » is in the position of nominative, khabar of inna.
The clause «نبيّن لكم ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the implied particle-maṣdar (أن).
The clause «نقرّ ... » has no grammatical position; it is a resumption clarifying what precedes.
The clause «نشاء ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the relative noun (ما).
The clause «نخرجكم ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause نقرّ.
The clause «تبلغوا ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the second particle-maṣdar (أن).
The clause «منكم من يتوفّى ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the implied clause نعمّركم.
The clause «يتوفّى ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the first relative noun (من).
The clause «منكم من يردّ ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause منكم من يتوفّى.
The clause «يردّ ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the second relative noun (من).
The clause «يعلم ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the particle-maṣdar (كي).
The clause «ترى ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the causal clause إنّا خلقناكم.
The clause «أنزلنا ... » is in the position of genitive, muḍāf ilayhi.
The clause «اهتزّت ... » has no grammatical position; it is the apodosis of a non-jussive condition.
The clause «ربت ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause اهتزّت.
The clause «أنبتت ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause اهتزّت.

* Morphology:
(البعث) is a samāʿī (heard-only) maṣdar of the triliteral verb بعث, on the wazn فَعْل with fatḥa then sukūn.
(علقة) is an inert noun for congealed blood, on the wazn فَعَلة with fatḥa on all three.
(مضغة) is an inert noun for a piece of flesh of the size that can be chewed, on the wazn فُعْلة with ḍamma, sukūn, then fatḥa.
(مخلّقة) is the feminine of مخلّق, the passive participle of the quadriliteral verb خلّق, on the wazn مُفَعَّل with ḍamma on the mīm and a fatḥa on the doubled ʿayn.
(طفلا) is a generic noun for the small creature that has not reached maturity, used for the singular and the plural, on the wazn فِعْل with kasra then sukūn.
(يتوفّى) contains a weak-letter change (iʿlāl) by substitution: its origin is يتوفّي, with a yāʾ at the end; the yāʾ was moved after a fatḥa and turned into an alif, and it is written in the form of the undotted yāʾ because it is fifth.
(هامدة) is the feminine of هامد, the active participle of the triliteral verb همد, on the wazn فاعل, the feminine being فاعلة.
(بهيج) is an assimilated adjective from بهج يبهج of the pattern فرح, on the wazn فعيل.

* Rhetoric:
1- The union of antithesis (ṭibāq) and equivalence (takāfuʾ):
Because one of the two opposites, or one of the two counterparts, comes literally and the other figuratively: the barrenness of the earth (humūd) and its stirring (ihtizāz) are opposites, because humūd is stillness and ihtizāz here is a particular movement, and both are figurative; swelling (rabw) and growing (inbāt) are opposites, and both are literal. We say this because the earth swells when water comes down on it, and it does not grow plants in that state; when the supply from the sky stops, and the air dries the moisture of the water, the swelling subsides and the earth returns to its level state, cracks open, and grows plants. So the beginning of the verse is takāfuʾ and its counterpart at the end is ṭibāq.
2- Rational figurative (al-majāz al-ʿaqlī):
In the words of the Exalted وَأَنْبَتَتْ مِنْ كُلِّ زَوْجٍ بَهِيجٍ, growing is attributed to the earth, which is a rational figurative, because the one who truly makes things grow is Allah the Exalted. Discussion of the figurative has come more than once.
We add here that the figurative is the opposite of the literal (ḥaqīqa); ḥaqīqa is of the pattern faʿīla in the sense of mafʿūla, from aḥaqqa al-amra yaḥuqquhu, if he established it, or from ḥaqqaqtuhu if you were certain of it, and the opposite of the figurative is so named because it is an established thing known by its indication. And majāz is of the pattern mafʿal from jāza al-shayʾa yajūzuhu, if he passed beyond it; so if the word is turned away from what the origin of the language requires, it is described as majāz, in that they passed beyond its original place with it, or it passed beyond the place where it was first put.

* Benefits:
- The proofs of His existence, the Exalted, are of two kinds:
a- Compound scientific proofs, which philosophers and theologians take as a means of demonstrating the temporal origination of the world and the eternity of Him, the Exalted. We have pointed to this kind of proof earlier.
b- Innate proofs (adilla fiṭriyya), perceived by the mind and the conscience together; this verse before us is of this kind, for Allah presented in it the stages of man's creation, from when he was a drop until he became a feeble old man at the edge of his grave. Whoever reflects on the development of human life realises that the One who created him and tended him in these stages is able to bring him back and resurrect him anew, and to hold him to account for what his hands earned, good for good and evil for evil, and that Allah is able to do all things.

safi-cedvel:6-7.t:
* I'rab:
(ذلك) is a demonstrative, mubtadaʾ «[Note: it may be the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, its implied form being "the matter is thus", and it may be an object of an omitted verb, its implied form being "We did that", with the bāʾ causal. Some, however, hold that the bāʾ is not causal but attached to something omitted that the context requires, the implied form being: "that which is mentioned bears witness that Allah is the Truth.." etc. And the maṣdars that follow are all conjoined to the first maṣdar, in the position of genitive.]», and the reference is to what has been mentioned from the beginning of creation to the last of the quickening of the earth..
The interpreted maṣdar (أنّ الله هو الحقّ..) is in the position of genitive through the bāʾ, attached to the khabar of the mubtadaʾ ذلك, and the bāʾ is causal.
(هو) is a detached pronoun, a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is (الحقّ); (على كلّ) is attached to (قدير), the khabar of anna.
The interpreted maṣdar (أنّه يحيي..) is in the position of genitive, conjoined to the first interpreted maṣdar.. and likewise the interpreted maṣdar (أنّه على كلّ شيء قدير).
The clause «ذلك بأنّ الله ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
The clause «هو الحقّ ... » is in the position of nominative, khabar of the (first) anna.
The clause «يحيي الموتى ... » is in the position of nominative, khabar of the (second) anna.
(الواو) is a conjunction, or resumptive; (لا) is the lā of generic negation; (ريب) is the ism of lā, indeclinable on fatḥa, in the position of accusative; (فيها) is attached to the khabar of lā; (الواو) is a conjunction; (في القبور) is attached to an omitted ṣila of من.
The interpreted maṣdar (أنّ الساعة آتية) is in the position of genitive, conjoined to the preceding interpreted maṣdar «[Note: or it is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, its implied form being "the matter is thus", the clause being resumptive.]».
The interpreted maṣdar (أنّ الله يبعث..) is in the position of genitive, conjoined to the interpreted maṣdar (أنّ الساعة آتية).
The clause «لا ريب فيها ... » is in the position of nominative, a second khabar of the particle (أنّ).
The clause «يبعث ... » is in the position of nominative, khabar of the last (أنّ).

safi-cedvel:8-10.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) is resumptive; (من الناس.. بغير علم) its i'rab has been given earlier «[Note: in verse (3) of this surah.]», (الواو) is a conjunction; (لا) is redundant, for emphasising the negation in both places; (هدى) is conjoined to علم, genitive, the sign of the genitive being an implied kasra on the alif, and likewise (كتاب)..
The clause «من الناس من ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
The clause «يجادل ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the relative noun (من).
(ثاني) is an accusative ḥāl from the agent of يجادل; (اللام) is the lām of causation; (يضلّ) is an imperfect verb, accusative through an implied an after the lām, and its object is omitted, i.e. "others"; (عن سبيل) is attached to (يضلّ); (له) is attached to an omitted fronted khabar; (في الدنيا) is attached to a ḥāl from خزي «[Note: or attached to the omitted khabar.]», (خزي) is a postponed mubtadaʾ, nominative; (الواو) is a conjunction; (يوم) is an accusative adverb attached to (نذيقه)..
The clause «يضلّ ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the implied particle-maṣdar (أن).
The interpreted maṣdar (أن يضلّ..) is in the position of genitive through the lām, attached to (ثاني عطفه).. or to (يجادل).
The clause «له.. خزي» has no grammatical position; it is an explanatory resumption.
The clause «نذيقه ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause له.. خزي.
(ذلك) is a mubtadaʾ «[Note: and see verse (6) of this surah.]», (بما) is attached to an omitted khabar, and (ما) is a relative with the returning pronoun omitted, i.e. "what your hands put forward"; (يداك) is the fāʿil of قدّمت, nominative, the sign of the nominative being the alif..
