and (الكاف) is the muḍāf ilayhi; (الواو) is a conjunction; (ظلّام) is genitive in form through the bāʾ, accusative in position, the khabar of laysa; (اللام) is redundant, for reinforcement; (العبيد) is genitive in form, accusative in position, direct object of the intensive form ظلّام «[Note: the preposition may be original, attached to the derived adjective ظلام, remaining as an indicator of reinforcement.]».
The clause «ذلك بما قدّمت ... » is in the position of accusative, the content of an implied saying, i.e. "saying to him: that is for what your hands put forward ...".
The clause «قدّمت يداك ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the relative noun (ما).
The clause «ليس بظلّام ... » is in the position of nominative, khabar of anna.
The interpreted maṣdar (أنّ الله ليس بظلّام..) is in the position of genitive, conjoined to the position of ما قدّمت and attached to what ما is attached to.

* Morphology:
(ثاني) is the active participle of the triliteral verb ثنى, on the wazn فاعل; the yāʾ is retained because it is in a construct.
(عطفه) is a noun for the side, right or left, i.e. the flank, on the wazn فِعْل with kasra then sukūn.

safi-cedvel:11-13.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) is resumptive; (من الناس من يعبد الله) the like of it has been parsed earlier «[Note: in verse (3) of this surah.]», (على حرف) is attached to a ḥāl, i.e. "resting on an edge" «[Note: the preposition and its genitive noun may themselves be the ḥāl, in the sense of "wavering" or "unsteady".]», (الفاء) is a conjunction of consequence; (أصابه) is a past verb, indeclinable on fatḥa, in the position of jussive, the protasis, and (الهاء) is the direct object; (اطمأنّ) is in the position of jussive, the apodosis; (به) is attached to (اطمأنّ); (انقلب) is in the position of jussive, the second apodosis; (على وجهه) is a ḥāl from the agent of انقلب, i.e. "disbelieving"; (ذلك) is a mubtadaʾ, the reference being to disbelief and apostasy; (هو) is a separation pronoun (ḍamīr faṣl) with no grammatical position «[Note: or a detached pronoun, mubtadaʾ whose khabar is الخسران, the clause هو الخسران being the khabar of the demonstrative.]», (الخسران) is the khabar of the mubtadaʾ ذلك..
The clause «من الناس من يعبد ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
The clause «يعبد ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the relative noun (من).
The clause «إن أصابه ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the resumptive clause.
The clause «اطمأنّ به ... » has no grammatical position; it is the apodosis of a jussive condition, not joined with the fāʾ.
The clause «إن أصابته فتنة ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause أصابه خير..
The clause «انقلب على وجهه» has no grammatical position; it is the apodosis of a jussive condition, not joined with the fāʾ.
The clause «خسر الدنيا» is in the position of accusative, a ḥāl «[Note: it may be a resumption with no grammatical position.. and it may be a badal for the clause انقلب.
(2, 3) Or it is in the position of accusative, an adjective of the indefinite described (ما).]».
The clause «ذلك.. الخسران ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
The agent of (يدعو) is a latent pronoun referring to من; (من دون) is attached to a ḥāl from (ما), which is the object of يدعو, and (لا) is negative in both places, and the second (ما) is conjoined to the first, in the position of accusative; (ذلك هو الضلال البعيد) is like ذلك هو الخسران المبين.
The clause «يدعو ... » has no grammatical position; it is an explanatory resumption.
The clause «يضرّه ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the relative noun (ما) «2».
The clause «ينفعه ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the second relative noun (ما) «3».
The clause «ذلك.. الضلال البعيد» has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
(اللام) in لمن is the lām of commencement «[Note: because (يدعو) is made to include the sense of "claims" (yazʿumu), which has the sense of saying together with belief, so the verb يدعو is suspended from operating by the lām. Abū l-Baqāʾ gave another analysis of يدعو, that it is a repetition of the first verb يدعو and so has no object.. and some made the lām redundant, which Ibn Hishām rejected, regarding it as extremely anomalous despite its acceptance by some of the parsers who measured it on His words: «ردف لكم» in verse (72) of surah al-Naml.]», (من) is a relative noun, indeclinable, in the position of nominative as a mubtadaʾ, and the khabar is omitted, its implied form being "his god"; (ضرّه) is a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is (أقرب); (من نفعه) is attached to (أقرب); (اللام) is the lām of oath, for an implied oath «[Note: or the lām of commencement, giving emphasis, the clause being resumptive or the khabar of (من) if no khabar is implied for it..]», and the specified subject of the dispraise (makhṣūṣ al-dhamm) is omitted, its implied form being "huwa".
The clause «يدعو ... » has no grammatical position; it is a resumption confirming the first.
The clause «من.. (إلهه)» is in the position of accusative, direct object of the verb يدعو, suspended from operating by the lām of commencement.
The clause «ضرّه أقرب ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the relative noun (من).
The clause «بئس المولى ... » has no grammatical position; it is the response to an implied oath.
The clause «بئس العشير ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the response to the oath.

* Morphology:
(حرف) is a noun for the extremity and edge of a thing, on the wazn فَعْل with fatḥa then sukūn.
(الخسران) is one of the samāʿī maṣdars of خسر, on the wazn فُعْلان with ḍamma then sukūn; the other maṣdars are: خَسْر with fatḥa or ḍamma on the khāʾ and sukūn on the sīn, خَسَر or خُسُر with two fatḥas or two ḍammas, خَسار with fatḥa on the khāʾ, and خَسارة with fatḥa on the khāʾ.
(العشير) is a noun for the tribe, the kinsman, or the companion, on the wazn فعيل, its plural being عشراء on the wazn فُعَلاء with ḍamma then fatḥa.

* Rhetoric:
Metaphor in the words of the Exalted ذلِكَ هُوَ الضَّلالُ الْبَعِيدُ: "far error" is borrowed from the error of one who has strayed far into the wilderness, so that the distance of his straying grew long and distant.

* Benefits:
- Two human portraits:
The first of them depicts a type of people afflicted with the disease of arrogance and conceit, joined to ignorance, so he rushes into disputation and argument in what he knows and what he does not know; it is enough ignorance for a man to speak about everything and poke his nose into every issue. This kind is almost entirely harm, with no benefit in it.
The second portrait depicts a group of people whose souls are weak and whose faith is weak, so they are always and forever as if on the brink of a pit, liable to fall into this pit as soon as they are exposed to a test or trial in person or property, turning back on their heels, having disbelieved in Allah and lost this world and the next. For that reason, patience in life under trial is one of the indicators of faith and one of its certain proofs.
2- يدعو لمن ضره أقرب من نفعه:
a- Among the grammarians are those who regarded this lām as the lām of commencement, and among them those who regarded it as the lām preparing for an oath, and among them those who hold that this lām was repeated for emphasis.
b- The acceptable view, which accords with the rules of grammar, is that this lām is redundant, entering the direct object «يدعو», especially since ʿAbdullāh read this verse without the lām of commencement, i.e. «يدعو من ضره». al-Jalāl al-Suyūṭī chose this view.
There are other opinions about this lām that are hardly to be counted, so we have passed over mentioning them.

safi-cedvel:14-14.t:
* I'rab:
(جنّات) is an accusative direct object whose governor is يدخل, the sign of the accusative being the kasra; (من تحتها) is attached to (تجري) «[Note: or attached to an omitted ḥāl from الأنهار.]» (ما) is a relative noun, indeclinable, in the position of accusative as direct object, with the returning pronoun omitted, i.e. "He wills it".
The clause «إنّ الله يدخل ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
The clause «يدخل ... » is in the position of nominative, khabar of inna.
The clause «آمنوا ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the relative noun (الذين).
The clause «عملوا ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the ṣila clause.
The clause «تجري ... الأنهار» is in the position of accusative, an adjective of جنّات.
The clause «إنّ الله يفعل ... » has no grammatical position; it is an explanatory resumption.
The clause «يفعل ما يريد» is in the position of nominative, khabar of inna.
The clause «يريد» has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the relative noun (ما).

safi-cedvel:15-15.t:
* I'rab:
(من) is a conditional noun, mubtadaʾ; (كان) is a defective past verb in the position of jussive, the protasis, and its ism is a pronoun referring to من; (أن) is the lightened form of the heavy (anna), and its ism is an omitted pronoun of the matter, and the third-person pronoun in (ينصره) refers to the Prophet ﷺ, because the flow of speech points to that; (في الدنيا) is attached to (ينصره); (الفاء) links the apodosis; (اللام) is the lām of command, and the agent of (يمدد) refers to the conditional noun من; (بسبب) is attached to (يمدد), and the bāʾ is for transitivity «[Note: some parsers allowed the bāʾ to be redundant, with (سبب) genitive in form, accusative in position, a direct object; and (وإلى السماء) is attached to (يمدد).]», (إلى السماء) is attached to an adjective of سبب; (ليقطع، لينظر) are like ليمدد; (هل) is an interrogative particle; (يذهبنّ) is an imperfect verb, indeclinable on fatḥa, in the position of nominative.. and (النون) is for emphasis; (ما) is a relative, direct object whose governor is يذهبنّ..
The clause «من كان ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
The clause «كان يظنّ ... » is in the position of nominative, khabar of the mubtadaʾ (من).
The clause «يظنّ ... » is in the position of accusative, khabar of kāna.
The clause «لن ينصره الله ... » is in the position of nominative, khabar of the lightened operative (أن).
The interpreted maṣdar (أن لن ينصره..) is in the position of accusative, standing in place of the two objects of يظنّ.
The clause «ليمدد ... » is in the position of jussive, apodosis of the condition, joined with the fāʾ.
The clause «ليقطع ... » is in the position of jussive, conjoined to the clause يمدد.
The clause «لينظر ... » is in the position of jussive, conjoined to the clause ليقطع.
The clause «هل يذهبنّ كيده ... » is in the position of accusative, direct object, its governor being ينظر, the verb having been suspended because of the interrogative.
The clause «يغيظ ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the relative noun (ما) «[Note: the returning pronoun is the latent pronoun that is the agent of يغيظ, and in it is a pronoun referring to من كان.. i.e. "what enrages him".]».

safi-cedvel:16-16.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) is resumptive; (كذلك) is attached to a ḥāl from the object pronoun in (أنزلناه) «[Note: i.e. "We sent it down as a guide thus".. It may also be attached to an omitted absolute object (mafʿūl muṭlaq)..]», (آيات) is an accusative ḥāl from the pronoun in (أنزلناه) «[Note: the ḥāl comes inert because it is qualified by an adjective.]», the sign of the accusative being the kasra; (الواو) is a conjunction, and the object of يريد is omitted, its implied form being: "He wills his guidance".
The interpreted maṣdar (أنّ الله يهدي ... ) is in the position of accusative, conjoined to the position of the hāʾ in (أنزلناه) «[Note: it may be in the position of nominative as khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, i.e.: "the matter is that Allah guides.."]».
The clause «أنزلناه ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
The clause «يهدي ... » is in the position of nominative, khabar of anna.
The clause «يريد» has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the relative noun (من).

safi-cedvel:17-17.t:
* I'rab:
(الصابئين) is conjoined to (الذين آمنوا) by the wāw, accusative, the sign of the accusative being the yāʾ, and the sign of the accusative in (النصارى) is the implied fatḥa on the alif; (بينهم) is an accusative adverb attached to (يفصل), and likewise (يوم); (على كلّ) is attached to (شهيد).
The clause «إنّ الذين ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
The clause «آمنوا ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the first relative noun (الذين).
The clause «هادوا ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the second relative noun (الذين).
The clause «أشركوا ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the third relative noun (الذين).
The clause «إنّ الله يفصل ... » is in the position of nominative, khabar of the first inna «[Note: it was said that the khabar is omitted, its implied form being "divided".. and the clause has no grammatical position, being an explanation of the omitted khabar.]».
The clause «يفصل بينهم ... » is in the position of nominative, khabar of the second inna.
The clause «إنّ الله.. شهيد» has no grammatical position; it is causal.

* Morphology:
(المجوس) is a generic collective noun for those who worship fire or the sun, and those who say that the world has two origins, light and darkness, on the wazn فَعول with fatḥa on the fāʾ.

* Benefits:
Opening the two clauses with inna:
In opening the two clauses with inna there is an increase in the emphasis of the speech, and the poets have watched it in their poetry. Jarīr said:
إن الخليفة إن الله سربله ... سربال ملك به تزجى الخواتيم
(The caliph, indeed Allah has clothed him in a garment of kingship, by which the ends are driven.)
His words "إن الله سربله" are the khabar of the first inna, and he repeated it to emphasise the emphasis. سربله means "clothed him" with the kingship likened to a garment (sirbāl). It is also related as "سربال ملك". His words «به» mean "by that clothing or kingship". «تزجى» means "are driven". «الخواتيم» is the plural of khātim, with fatḥa or kasra, and the original is khawātim, so the yāʾ was added; what is meant by it is the outcomes of praiseworthy affairs and their ends. Abū Ḥayyān said: "It is possible that the khabar of «إن» is his words به تزجى الخواتيم, and the clause إن الله سربله is parenthetical." It is also related as ترجى with an undotted rāʾ.

safi-cedvel:18-18.t:
* I'rab:
(الهمزة) is for interrogation; (له) is attached to (يسجد); (في السموات) is attached to an omitted ṣila of من, and likewise (في الأرض) for the second relative; (من الناس) is attached to an adjective of (كثير) «[Note: (كثير) may be conjoined to (من في السموات), and it may be a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is omitted, its implied form being "rewarded".]», (عليه) is attached to (حقّ); (من) is a conditional noun, a fronted direct object; (يهن) is jussive, the protasis, the sign of the jussive being the sukūn, and it was vowelled with kasra because of the meeting of two quiescent letters; (الفاء) links the apodosis; (ما) is negative, inoperative; (له) is attached to an omitted fronted khabar; (مكرم) is genitive in form, nominative in position, a postponed mubtadaʾ.
The interpreted maṣdar (أنّ الله يسجد له) is in the position of accusative, standing in place of the two objects of ترى.
The clause «لم تر ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
The clause «يسجد ... » is in the position of nominative, khabar of anna.
The clause «حقّ عليه العذاب» is in the position of nominative, an adjective of كثير «[Note: the clause may be the khabar of the second mubtadaʾ (كثير), the adjective having been omitted because the first indicates it, i.e.: "many of mankind". al-ʿUkbarī put this view ahead of the other view above.]».
The clause «من يهن الله ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
The clause «ما له من مكرم ... » is in the position of jussive, apodosis of the condition, joined with the fāʾ.
The clause «إنّ الله يفعل ... » has no grammatical position; it is an explanatory resumption.
The clause «يفعل ما يشاء ... » is in the position of nominative, khabar of inna.
The clause «يشاء ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the relative noun (ما).

* Morphology:
(يهن) contains a weak-letter change by deletion for the sake of the jussive: its origin is يهين; two quiescent letters met, so the yāʾ, which is converted from a wāw, was dropped; its wazn is يفل, with ḍamma then kasra.
(مكرم) is the active participle of the quadriliteral verb أكرم, on the wazn مُفعِل with ḍamma on the mīm and kasra on the ʿayn «[Translator's note: translated as written in the source; in the verse the form مكرم is understood as a passive participle (honoured), as the sense requires.]».

safi-cedvel:19-22.t:
* I'rab:
(في ربّهم) is attached to (اختصموا) with an omitted muḍāf, i.e. "concerning the religion of their Lord"; (الفاء) is a conjunction of consequence; (لهم) is attached to the passive verb قطّعت; (من نار) is attached to an adjective of (ثياب); (من فوق) is attached to the passive verb يصبّ; (به) is attached to the passive verb يصهر, and (ما) is a relative, the nāʾib fāʿil, in the position of nominative, and (الجلود) is conjoined to it by the conjunction «[Note: it may be the nāʾib fāʿil of an omitted verb, i.e. "are burnt".]», (في بطونهم) is attached to an omitted ṣila of ما.
The clause «هذان خصمان ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
The clause «اختصموا ... » is in the position of nominative, an adjective of (خصمان) «[Note: the verb came in the plural because (خصمان) are two parties, and a party comprises individuals.]».
The clause «الذين كفروا ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the resumptive clause.
The clause «كفروا ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the relative noun (الذين).
The clause «قطّعت لهم ثياب» is in the position of nominative, khabar of the mubtadaʾ (الذين).
The clause «يصبّ.. الحميم» is in the position of accusative, a ḥāl from the hāʾ in (لهم) «[Note: or it is a second khabar of the mubtadaʾ (الذين).]».
The clause «يصهر ما في بطونهم» is in the position of accusative, a ḥāl from الحميم.
(الواو) is a conjunction; (لهم) is attached to an omitted fronted khabar; (من حديد) is attached to an adjective of (مقامع), the mubtadaʾ.
The clause «لهم مقامع ... » is in the position of accusative, conjoined to the clause يصبّ «[Note: or resumptive, confirming the meaning of the preceding clauses.]».
(كلّما) is an adverb meaning "when", containing the sense of a condition, attached to the apodosis أعيدوا..
(منها) is attached to (يخرجوا); (من غمّ) is a badal for the preceding genitive, by repeating the preposition «[Note: the preposition (من) may be causal, and so attached to (يخرجوا), i.e. "that they come out because of the distress".]», (فيها) is attached to the passive verb (أعيدوا).
The clause «أرادوا ... » is in the position of genitive, with (كلّما) annexed to it «[Note: it is possible in (كلّما) that (كلّ) is an adverb, because it is annexed to an adverb, and (ما) a maṣdar adverbial particle, the interpreted maṣdar ما (أرادوا ... ) being in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi, i.e.: "every time of wanting ..."]».
The clause «يخرجوا ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the particle-maṣdar (أن).
The clause «أعيدوا فيها» has no grammatical position; it is the apodosis of a non-jussive condition.
The clause «ذوقوا ... » is in the position of accusative, the content of an implied saying, i.e.: "the angels say to them: Taste..".

* Morphology:
(خصمان) is the dual of خصم, which is originally a maṣdar that by right should be singular and masculine; it may be used as an adjective, as it comes here, and then be dualised and pluralised; its wazn is فَعْل with fatḥa then sukūn.
(مقامع) is the plural of مقمعة, a noun of instrument with which one subdues, i.e. strikes; its wazn is مِفعلة with kasra on the mīm and fatḥa on the ʿayn.

* Rhetoric:
Representative metaphor:
In the words of the Exalted فَالَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا قُطِّعَتْ لَهُمْ ثِيابٌ مِنْ نارٍ. It is as if the preparation of the fire surrounding them is likened to cutting garments and tailoring them for them to the measure of their bodies. So in the speech there is a mocking representative metaphor; there is neither cutting nor real garments, and the gathering of the garments for the bodies is as if by the piling up of the fire surrounding them, some of it above some.

* Benefits:
- كلّما:
It is «كل» to which the adverbial maṣdar «ما» has been attached.
There is an opinion that «ما» is an indefinite noun with an adjective, meaning "time", so it gives repetition, as in «كُلَّما رُزِقُوا مِنْها مِنْ ثَمَرَةٍ رِزْقاً قالُوا». Likewise this verse «كُلَّما أَرادُوا أَنْ يَخْرُجُوا مِنْها مِنْ غَمٍّ أُعِيدُوا فِيها»; the repetition is perceived from the meaning. It enters only upon the past verb, and it is indeclinable on fatḥa, in the position of accusative as an adverb; it is made accusative by its apodosis, and its apodosis is also a past verb ...

safi-cedvel:23-24.t:
* I'rab:
(إنّ الله.. الأنهار) its i'rab has been given earlier «[Note: in verse (14) of this surah.]», (فيها) is attached to the passive verb (يحلّون); (من أساور) is attached to an adjective of an omitted object, since يحلّون is made to include the sense of "are made to wear", i.e. "they are adorned with ornaments of bracelets" «[Note: al-Akhfash allows (من) to be redundant after an affirmative, so (أساور) would be genitive in form, accusative in position, a direct object..
or (من) is partitive, and the preposition is attached to (يحلّون).]», (من ذهب) is attached to an adjective of (أساور); (الواو) is a conjunction; (لؤلؤا) is conjoined to the omitted object «[Note: or conjoined to the position of أساور if (من) is parsed as redundant.]», (فيها) is attached to a ḥāl from (حرير), an adjective that precedes the described.
The clause «إنّ الله يدخل ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
The clause «يدخل ... » is in the position of nominative, khabar of inna, and the clause «آمنوا ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the relative noun (الذين).
The clause «عملوا ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the ṣila clause.
The clause «تجري.. الأنهار» is in the position of accusative, an adjective of جنّات.
The clause «يحلّون فيها ... » is in the position of accusative, a ḥāl from the relative noun, or from جنّات; and the clause «لباسهم.. حرير» is in the position of accusative, conjoined to the clause يحلّون.
(الواو) is a conjunction; (إلى الطيّب) is attached to (هدوا); (من القول) is a ḥāl from الطيّب; (إلى صراط) is attached to (هدوا).
The clause «هدوا (the first) ... » is in the position of accusative, conjoined to the clause يحلّون.
The clause «هدوا (the second) ... » is in the position of accusative, conjoined to the first clause هدوا.

* Morphology:
(لؤلؤا) is an inert noun for the well-known precious stone, on the wazn فُعلُل with ḍamma on the fāʾ and on the first lām.
(حرير) is an inert noun for the well-known cloth, on the wazn فَعيل with fatḥa on the fāʾ.

safi-cedvel:25-25.t:
* I'rab:
The khabar of (إنّ) is omitted, its implied form being "tormented", or "losers", or "perishing"; (الواو) is a conjunction, or circumstantial; (عن سبيل) is attached to (يصدّون); (المسجد) is conjoined to سبيل by the wāw, genitive; (الذي) is a relative noun in the position of genitive, a second adjective of المسجد «[Note: it may be in the position of nominative as khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, its implied form being "huwa".. the clause being an explanatory resumption..
and it may be an object of an omitted verb, its implied form being "aʿnī" (I mean).]» (للناس) is attached to (جعلنا) «[Note: or attached to an omitted second direct object, i.e. "a qibla for the people".]», i.e. "for the sake of the people"; (سواء) is a maṣdar in the position of ḥāl; (العاكف) is the fāʿil of سواء, nominative; (فيه) is attached to (العاكف); (الباد) is conjoined to العاكف by the wāw, nominative, the sign of the nominative being the implied ḍamma on the omitted yāʾ, in observance of the reading, in continuation and in pause; (الواو) is resumptive; (من) is a conditional noun, mubtadaʾ; (فيه) is attached to (يرد); (بإلحاد) is attached to a ḥāl from the omitted object of يرد, i.e. "he intends transgression, being involved in deviation" «[Note: some parsers allowed the bāʾ to be redundant, so (إلحاد) would be genitive in form, accusative in position, a direct object whose governor is يرد.]», (بظلم) is a badal for إلحاد by repeating the preposition «[Note: or a second ḥāl.. and the bāʾ may be causal and so attached to إلحاد.]», (من عذاب) is attached to (نذقه), and (من) is partitive.
The clause «إنّ الذين ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
The clause «كفروا ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the relative noun (الذين).
The clause «يصدّون ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the ṣila clause «[Note: either by taking يصدّون in the sense of صدّوا, or by taking كفروا in the sense of يكفرون.. The clause may be circumstantial, by taking the clause to be the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, i.e. "they bar", the nominal clause then being a ḥāl; or on the redundancy of the wāw before an affirmative imperfect, in which case the verbal clause is the ḥāl.]».
The clause «جعلناه ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the relative noun (الذي).
The clause «من يرد ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
The clause «يرد فيه بإلحاد ... » is in the position of nominative, khabar of the mubtadaʾ (من) «[Note: the khabar may be the two clauses of the condition and the apodosis together.]».
The clause «نذقه ... » has no grammatical position; it is the apodosis of a jussive condition, not joined with the fāʾ.

* Morphology:
(الباد) is the active participle of بدا, i.e. he went out to the desert, on the wazn فاعل; the dropping of the yāʾ is not iʿlāl but observance of the reading in continuation and in pause; it also contains a weak-letter change by substitution: the origin is البادو, with a wāw at the end, because the imperfect is يبدو; the wāw was moved after a kasra and turned into a yāʾ, so it became البادي.
(إلحاد) is the regular maṣdar of the quadriliteral verb ألحد, i.e. he deviated from the right course or did wrong, on the wazn إفعال with kasra on the hamza.

safi-cedvel:26-29.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) is resumptive; (إذ) is an adverbial noun in the position of accusative, direct object of an omitted verb, its implied form being "udhkur" (remember); (لإبراهيم) is attached to (بوّأنا), which is made to include the sense of "We prepared" «[Note: and (اللام) is redundant if (بوّأنا) is made to include the sense of "We settled".. In al-Qurṭubī: and it was said: بوّأنا لإبراهيم..
i.e. "We showed him its foundation so that he might build it". al-ʿUkbarī said the lām is redundant, citing in evidence His words: «ولقد بوّأنا بني إسرائيل ... ».]», (مكان) is an accusative adverb of place attached to (بوّأنا) «[Note: or it is a direct object of the verb بوّأنا, made to include the sense of a transitive verb.]», (أن) is explicative (tafsīriyya) «[Note: some parsers said (أن) is redundant, which is weak.]», (لا) is prohibitive, jussive; (بي) is attached to (تشرك); (للطائفين) is attached to (طهّر); (السجود) is a badal for الركّع, genitive.
The clause «بوّأنا ... » is in the position of genitive, muḍāf ilayhi.
The clause «لا تشرك بي ... » has no grammatical position; it is explicative, with بوّأنا made to include the sense of "We made clear".
The clause «طهّر ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the explicative clause.
(الواو) is a conjunction; (في الناس) is attached to (أذّن); (بالحجّ) is attached to (أذّن); (يأتوك) is an imperfect verb, jussive as the response to a request, the sign of the jussive being the dropping of the nūn..
and (الكاف) is the direct object, and (الواو) the agent; (رجالا) is an accusative ḥāl from the agent of يأتوك; (على كلّ) is attached to an omitted ḥāl, i.e. "riding on every lean camel"; (يأتين) is indeclinable on sukūn, in the position of nominative.. and (النون) is the agent, a pronoun returning to الضوامر; (من كلّ) is attached to (يأتين); (عميق) is an adjective of فجّ, genitive like it.
The clause «أذّن ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause طهّر.
The clause «يأتوك ... » has no grammatical position; it is the apodosis of an implied condition, not joined with the fāʾ.
The clause «يأتين ... » is in the position of genitive, an adjective of كلّ ضامر.
(اللام) is for causation; (يشهدوا) is an imperfect verb, accusative through an implied an after the lām, the sign of the accusative being the dropping of the nūn.. and (الواو) is the agent; (لهم) is attached to an adjective of (منافع).
The interpreted maṣdar (أن يشهدوا ... ) is in the position of genitive through the lām, attached to (يأتوك); (يذكروا) is accusative, conjoined to (يشهدوا); (في أيّام) is attached to (يذكروا); (ما) is a relative noun in the position of genitive through the preposition, attached to (يذكروا) «[Note: it was said: the mention is during the slaughter; and it was said: (على) indicates causality.]», (من بهيمة) is attached to an omitted ḥāl from the second object, i.e. "He provided it to them, being of the cattle quadrupeds"; (الفاء) links the apodosis of an implied condition; (منها) is attached to (كلوا)..
The clause «يشهدوا ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the implied particle-maṣdar (أن).
The clause «يذكروا ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause يشهدوا.
The clause «رزقهم ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the relative noun (ما).
The clause «كلوا ... » is in the position of jussive, apodosis of an implied condition, i.e.: "if eating is sound, then eat ...".
The clause «أطعموا ... » is in the position of jussive, conjoined to the clause كلوا ...
(اللام) is the lām of command in the three places; (بالبيت) is attached to (يطّوّفوا).
The clause «يقضوا ... » is conjoined to the clause أطعموا.
The clause «يوفوا ... » is conjoined to the clause يقضوا.
The clause «يطّوّفوا ... » is conjoined to the clause يقضوا.

* Morphology:
(ضامر) is the active participle of ضمر يضمر, of the pattern of naṣara and of karuma, on the wazn فاعل.
(عميق) is an assimilated adjective from عمق يعمق of the pattern of karuma, and عمق يعمق of the pattern of fariḥa, on the wazn فعيل, meaning "distant".
(البائس) is the active participle of بئس يبأس of the pattern of fariḥa, on the wazn فاعل.
(تفثهم) is a noun for the dirt of the nails and the like, on the wazn فَعَل with two fatḥas.
(العتيق) is an assimilated adjective from عتق يعتق of the pattern of naṣara, on the wazn فعيل.

* Benefits:
1- البيت العتيق:
There are sayings about it: the most preferred is that it is the ancient house, because it is the first house established for the people, that they might take from it rites that bring them nearer to Allah ...
2- The lām of command:
It is the lām that jusses the imperfect, placed for requesting, and its vowel is kasra, as in «لينفق ذو سعة من سعته». Its being made quiescent after the fāʾ and the wāw is more frequent than vowelling it, as in «فليستجيبوا لي وليؤمنوا بي»; it may also be made quiescent after thumma, as in «ثم ليقضوا تفثهم».
Important note: there is no means to command with the passive verb except the lām, whether for the first, second or third person, as in «لتعن بحاجتي» and «ليعن زيد بالأمر» and «لأكرم من قبلك».
There are other minor matters about it, to which one refers in the longer works.

safi-cedvel:30-31.t:
* I'rab:
(ذلك) is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, its implied form being "the matter" or "the affair"; (الواو) is a conjunction; (من) is a conditional noun that jusses, in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ; (الفاء) links the apodosis; (له) is attached to (خير), the khabar; (عند) is an accusative adverb attached to (خير); (الواو) is resumptive; (لكم) is attached to the passive verb (أحلّت); (الأنعام) is the nāʾib fāʿil, nominative; (إلّا) is a particle of exception; (ما) is a relative noun in the position of accusative as a discontinuous exception (istithnāʾ munqaṭiʿ), and it was said continuous; (عليكم) is attached to the passive verb (يتلى), and the nāʾib fāʿil is a latent pronoun referring to the verses of prohibition, which the relative ما indicates; (الفاء) links the response to an implied condition; (من الأوثان) is attached to a ḥāl from (الرجس).
The clause «(الأمر) ذلك ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
The clause «من يعظّم ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
The clause «يعظّم ... » is in the position of nominative, khabar of the mubtadaʾ (من).
The clause «هو خير له ... » is in the position of jussive, apodosis of the condition, joined with the fāʾ.
The clause «أحلّت.. الأنعام» has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
The clause «يتلى ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the relative noun (ما).
The clause «اجتنبوا ... » is in the position of jussive, apodosis of an implied condition, i.e.: "if you want good, then avoid".
The clause «اجتنبوا (the second)» is conjoined to the clause اجتنبوا (the first).
(حنفاء) is an accusative ḥāl from the agent pronoun of (اجتنبوا); (لله) is attached to (حنفاء); (غير) is a second ḥāl, confirming, accusative; (به) is attached to (مشركين); (الواو) is a conjunction; (من يشرك) is like من يعظّم; (بالله) is attached to (يشرك); (الفاء) links the apodosis; (كأنّما) is kāffa and makfūfa; (من السماء) is attached to (خرّ); (الفاء) is a conjunction; (به) is attached to (تهوي); (في مكان) is attached to (تهوي).
The clause «من يشرك ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause من يعظّم.
The clause «يشرك بالله ... » is in the position of nominative, khabar of the mubtadaʾ (من).
The clause «كأنما خرّ من السماء» is in the position of jussive, apodosis of the condition, joined with the fāʾ.
The clause «تخطفه الطير ... » is in the position of nominative, khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, its implied form being "huwa"..
and the nominal clause is in the position of jussive, conjoined to the clause كأنما خرّ من السماء.
The clause «تهوي به الريح» is in the position of nominative, conjoined to the clause تخطفه.

* Morphology:
(الأوثان) is the plural of وثن, an inert noun for the stone carved for worship, on the wazn فَعَل with two fatḥas.
(الزور) is a noun from الزور or الازورار, which is deviation in both, on the wazn فُعْل with ḍamma then sukūn.
(حنفاء) is the plural of حنيف, an assimilated adjective from حنف يحنف of the pattern of ḍaraba, i.e. he inclined to the religion of Islam, on the wazn فعيل, and the wazn of حنفاء is فُعَلاء with ḍamma then fatḥa.
(سحيق) is an assimilated adjective from سحق يسحق of the pattern of fariḥa and of karuma, i.e. he was far, on the wazn فعيل.

* Rhetoric:
Compound simile (al-tashbīh al-murakkab):
In the words of the Exalted وَمَنْ يُشْرِكْ بِاللَّهِ فَكَأَنَّما خَرَّ مِنَ السَّماءِ فَتَخْطَفُهُ الطَّيْرُ أَوْ تَهْوِي بِهِ الرِّيحُ فِي مَكانٍ سَحِيقٍ. It is as if He, glory be to Him, said: whoever associates others with Allah has destroyed himself with a destruction after which there is none, by portraying his state with the state of one who fell from the sky, and the birds snatched him and he was scattered in pieces in their crops, or the wind blew him away until it cast him down in some distant place of casting.

safi-cedvel:32-32.t:
* I'rab:
(ذلك.. شعائر الله) is like ذلك.. حرمات الله «[Note: in verse (30) of this surah.]», (الفاء) links the apodosis, and the pronoun in (إنّها) refers to الشعائر «[Note: there is an omitted muḍāf, i.e. "for revering them is part of the piety of hearts".]», (من تقوى) is attached to the khabar of inna, and the sign of the genitive is the implied kasra on the alif.
The clause «(الأمر) ذلك ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
The clause «من يعظّم ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
The clause «يعظّم ... » is in the position of nominative, khabar of the mubtadaʾ (من).
The clause «إنّها من تقوى ... » is in the position of jussive, apodosis of the condition, joined with the fāʾ.

* Benefits:
- His words, the Exalted, فَإِنَّها مِنْ تَقْوَى الْقُلُوبِ: this question has been raised: why was the pronoun of «فإنها» made feminine? The answer: because there is an omitted muḍāf, the implied form being: "for this practice, or trait, or conduct, or act of obedience, is part of the piety of hearts".

safi-cedvel:33-33.t:
* I'rab:
(لكم) is attached to a fronted khabar; (فيها) is attached to a ḥāl from (منافع) «[Note: or attached to the omitted khabar.]», (إلى أجل) is attached to an adjective of منافع, its implied form being "deferred" or "appointed"; (إلى البيت) is attached to an omitted khabar of the mubtadaʾ (محلّها).
The clause «لكم فيها منافع ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive, or causal.
The clause «محلّها إلى البيت ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the resumptive clause.

safi-cedvel:34-35.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) is resumptive; (لكلّ) is attached to an omitted second direct object whose governor is جعلنا; (اللام) is for causation; (يذكروا) is accusative through an implied an after the lām.
The interpreted maṣdar (أن يذكروا ... ) is in the position of genitive through the lām, attached to (جعلنا).
(يذكروا.. بهيمة الأنعام) its i'rab has been given earlier «[Note: in verse (28) of this surah.]», (الفاء) the first is resumptive, and the second links the apodosis of an implied condition; (له) is attached to (أسلموا), and (الواو) is a conjunction.
The clause «جعلنا ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
The clause «يذكروا ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the implied particle-maṣdar (أن).
The clause «رزقهم ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the relative noun (ما).
The clause «إلهكم إله ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
The clause «أسلموا ... » is in the position of jussive, apodosis of an implied condition, i.e. "if you seek His good pleasure, submit to Him".
The clause «بشّر المخبتين» is conjoined to the clause أسلموا «[Note: the clause may be a resumption, with no grammatical position.]»..
(الذين) is a relative in the position of accusative, an adjective of (المخبتين) «[Note: or in the position of nominative as khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, its implied form being "hum".. or in the position of accusative as direct object of an omitted verb, its implied form being "amdaḥu" (I praise) or "aʿnī" (I mean).]», (إذا) is an adverb of future time attached to the apodosis وجلت; (الواو) is a conjunction in the three places; (الصابرين، المقيمي) are two nouns conjoined to المخبتين, accusative like it, the sign of the accusative in both being the yāʾ; (الصلاة) is a muḍāf ilayhi, genitive; (ممّا) is attached to (ينفقون), and the returning pronoun is omitted, i.e. "We provided it to them".
The clause «the condition, its protasis and its apodosis» has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the relative noun الذين.
The clause «ذكر الله» is in the position of genitive, muḍāf ilayhi.
The clause «وجلت قلوبهم» has no grammatical position; it is the apodosis of a condition.
The clause «أصابهم» has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the relative noun (ما).
The clause «رزقناهم» has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the second relative noun (ما).
The clause «ينفقون» has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the ṣila clause of الذين.

* Morphology:
(المخبتين) is the plural of المخبت, the active participle of the quadriliteral verb أخبت, meaning "he was humble and obedient"; al-ikhbāt is descending into the khabt, which is the low-lying ground.

safi-cedvel:36-36.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) is resumptive; (البدن) is a direct object of an omitted verb, its implied form being "jaʿalnā" (We made); (لكم) is attached to (جعلناها); (من شعائر) is attached to an omitted second direct object; the second (لكم) is attached to a fronted khabar; (فيها) is attached to a ḥāl from the mubtadaʾ (خير) «[Note: it may be attached to the omitted khabar; and see verse (33) of this surah.]», (الفاء) links the apodosis of an implied condition; (عليها) is attached to (اذكروا); (صوافّ) is an accusative ḥāl from the hāʾ in (عليها); (الفاء) is a conjunction, and the second (الفاء) links the apodosis of the condition, attached to (كلوا); (الواو) is a conjunction in both places; (كذلك) is attached to an omitted absolute object whose governor is سخّرناها; (لكم) is attached to (سخّرناها); (لعلّكم) is a particle resembling the verb, for hope.
The clause «(جعلنا) البدن ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
The clause «جعلناها (the aforementioned)» has no grammatical position; it is explicative.
The clause «لكم ... خير» is in the position of accusative, a ḥāl from the third-person pronoun in (جعلناها) «[Note: it may be a resumption to confirm what precedes it.]».
The clause «اذكروا ... » is in the position of jussive, apodosis of an implied condition, i.e. "if you slaughter them, then mention..".
The clause «وجبت جنوبها ... » is in the position of genitive, muḍāf ilayhi; and the clause «كلوا ... » has no grammatical position; it is the apodosis of a non-jussive condition.
The clause «أطعموا ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause كلوا; and the clause «سخّرناها ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
The clause «لعلّكم تشكرون ... » has no grammatical position; it is an explanatory resumption, or causal; and the clause «تشكرون» is in the position of nominative, khabar of لعلّكم.

* Morphology:
(البدن) is the plural of بدنة, a noun of a thing for the she-camel, on the wazn فَعَلة with fatḥas, and the wazn of البدن is فُعْل with ḍamma then sukūn.
(صوافّ) is the plural of صافّة, the active participle of the triliteral verb صفّ, on the wazn فاعل; its ʿayn and lām were assimilated because they are of the same letter, and the wazn of صوافّ is فواعل.
(القانع) is the active participle of the triliteral verb قنع, i.e. one who is content with little and with what is given, or one who asks people, of the pattern of fataḥa, on the wazn فاعل.
(المعترّ) is the active participle of the quinquiliteral verb اعترّ, i.e. one who presents himself without asking, on the wazn مفتعل with ḍamma on the mīm and kasra on the ʿayn; the kasra does not show on it because of the doubling, and the form is also a passive participle.

safi-cedvel:37-37.t:
* I'rab:
(الله) the exalted name is a fronted direct object, and (لحومها) is the fāʿil, nominative; (لا) is redundant, for emphasising the negation; (لكن) is a particle of rectification, inoperative; (التقوى) is the fāʿil of يناله, nominative, the sign of the nominative being the implied ḍamma on the alif; (منك) is attached to a ḥāl from التقوى; (كذلك سخّرها لكم) is like كذلك سخّرناها لكم «[Note: in the preceding verse (36).]», (اللام) is for causation; (تكبّروا) is an imperfect verb, accusative through an implied an after the lām.
The interpreted maṣdar (أن تكبّروا ... ) is in the position of genitive, attached to (سخّرها).
(ما) is a maṣdar particle «[Note: or a relative noun with the returning pronoun omitted.]», (الواو) is resumptive.
The interpreted maṣdar (ما هداكم ... ) is in the position of genitive through (على), attached to (تكبّروا) because it contains the sense of "give thanks".
The clause «لن ينال ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
The clause «يناله التقوى ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the resumptive clause.
The clause «سخّرها..» has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
The clause «تكبّروا ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the implied particle-maṣdar (أن).
The clause «هداكم ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the particle-maṣdar (ما), or of the relative noun.
The clause «بشّر ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.

* Morphology:
(لحوم) is the plural of لحم, an inert noun for what clothes the bones in animals and man, on the wazn فَعْل with fatḥa then sukūn, and the wazn of لحوم is فُعول with ḍamma on the fāʾ.

safi-cedvel:38-38.t:
* I'rab:
(عن الذين) is attached to (يدافع); (لا) is negative; (كفور) is an adjective of خوّان, genitive.
The clause «إنّ الله يدافع ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
The clause «يدافع ... » is in the position of nominative, khabar of inna.
The clause «آمنوا ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the relative noun (الذين).
The clause «إنّ الله لا يحبّ ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
The clause «لا يحبّ ... » is in the position of nominative, khabar of the second inna.

safi-cedvel:39-41.t:
* I'rab:
(للذين) the preposition and its genitive noun are the nāʾib fāʿil of the passive verb أذن; (يقاتلون) is an imperfect passive verb, nominative.. and (الواو) is the nāʾib fāʿil, and likewise the (الواو) in ظلموا.
The interpreted maṣdar (أنّهم ظلموا ... ) is in the position of genitive through the bāʾ, attached to (أذن), and the (الباء) is causal, "permission was given them to fight".
(الواو) is a conjunction; (على نصرهم) is attached to (قدير), and (اللام) is the shifted lām, for emphasis.
The clause «أذن للذين ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
The clause «يقاتلون ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the relative noun (الذين).
The clause «ظلموا ... » is in the position of nominative, khabar of anna.
The clause «إنّ الله ... لقدير» has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause أذن.
(الذين) is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, its implied form being "hum" «[Note: it may be in the position of genitive as a badal for the preceding relative (عن الذين آمنوا), verse 38, or for the second relative (للذين يقاتلون), verse 39.. and it may be in the position of accusative as direct object of an omitted verb, its implied form being "aʿnī" (I mean).]», and the (الواو) in (أخرجوا) is the nāʾib fāʿil; (من ديارهم) is attached to (أخرجوا); (بغير) is attached to a ḥāl from the nāʾib fāʿil «[Note: meaning "wronged".]», (إلّا) is a particle of exception..
The interpreted maṣdar (أن يقولوا ... ) is in the position of accusative as a discontinuous exception «[Note: the saying is excepted from the expulsion.. al-Suyūṭī made the exception a "emptied" one (mufarragh) by implication, i.e.: "they were not expelled from their homes for anything except their saying 'Our Lord is Allah'", so the interpreted maṣdar is in the position of genitive through an omitted preposition.]».
(الواو) is resumptive; (لولا) is a particle of prevention due to existence; (دفع) is a mubtadaʾ, nominative, whose khabar is omitted, its implied form being "existing"; (الناس) is the direct object of the maṣdar دفع; (بعضهم) is a badal for الناس, accusative; (ببعض) is attached to (دفع); (اللام) occurs in the response to لولا; (صوامع) is the nāʾib fāʿil of the verb هدّمت; (فيها) is attached to (يذكر); (اسم) is the nāʾib fāʿil of the verb يذكر; (كثيرا) is an absolute object standing in for the maṣdar, so it is its adjective, i.e. "much mention"; (الواو) is resumptive; (اللام) is the lām of oath for an implied oath; (ينصرنّ) is an imperfect verb, indeclinable on fatḥa, in the position of nominative; (من) is a relative noun, direct object, in the position of accusative; (إنّ الله لقويّ) is like إنّ الله.. لقدير; (عزيز) is a second khabar.
The clause «(هم) الذين أخرجوا ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
The clause «أخرجوا ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the relative noun (الذين).
The clause «يقولوا ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the particle-maṣdar (أن).
The clause «ربّنا الله ... » is in the position of accusative, the content of the saying.
The clause «لولا دفع الله ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
The clause «هدّمت صوامع ... » has no grammatical position; it is the apodosis of a non-jussive condition.
The clause «يذكر فيها اسم الله» is in the position of nominative, an adjective of مساجد and of what precedes it.
The clause «ينصرنّ الله ... » has no grammatical position; it is the response to an implied oath.
The clause «ينصره ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the relative noun (من).
The clause «إنّ الله لقويّ ... » has no grammatical position; it has the ruling of a causal clause.
(الّذين) admits what was admitted in the one before it; (مكّنّاهم) is a past verb, indeclinable on sukūn, in the position of jussive, the protasis; (في الأرض) is attached to (مكّنّاهم); (عن المنكر) is attached to (نهوا); (الواو) is resumptive; (لله) is attached to an omitted fronted khabar..
The clause «(هم) الذين ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
The clause «إن مكّنّاهم ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the relative noun (الذين).
The clause «أقاموا ... » has no grammatical position; it is the apodosis of a jussive condition, not joined with the fāʾ «[Note: the verb (أقاموا) is a past verb in the position of jussive, the apodosis.]».
The clause «آتوا ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause أقاموا.
The clause «أمروا ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause أقاموا.
The clause «نهوا ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause أقاموا; and the clause «لله عاقبة الأمور ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.

* Morphology:
(صوامع) is the plural of صومعة, a noun for a tall building, vaulted at the top, on the wazn فوعلة; it is a place of worship for monks, and it was said to be the place of devotion of the Sabians. The wazn of صوامع is فواعل.
(بيع) is the plural of بيعة, a noun for the place of worship of the Christians in the towns, on the wazn فَعلة with fatḥa then sukūn, and the wazn of بيع is فِعَل with kasra then fatḥa.
(صلوات) is the plural of صلاة, a noun for the church; it was said to be an Arabised word whose origin in Hebrew is صلوثا, with fatḥa on the ṣād and the thāʾ, shortened.
(نهوا) contains a weak-letter change by deletion: its origin is نهاوا, with the separating alif; two quiescent letters met, the lām of the word and the agent pronoun; the lām was dropped and what precedes it was given fatḥa to indicate it; its wazn is فعوا, with fatḥa on the fāʾ and the ʿayn.

* Benefits:
1- لولا:
It has been mentioned earlier that «لولا and لو ما» have two uses:
The first: that they indicate the prevention of their response due to the existence of what follows them, and in this case they are specific to nominal clauses, as in this verse «وَلَوْلا دَفْعُ اللَّهِ النَّاسَ» etc.
The second: that they indicate urging (takhṣīṣ), and in this case they are specific to verbal clauses, as in «لَوْلا أُنْزِلَ عَلَيْنَا الْمَلائِكَةُ».
Note: the khabar of the mubtadaʾ after «lawlā of prevention» must be omitted, because it is known from the flow of speech; likewise the response of lawlā is prevented because of the existence of its ism; the demolition of the monasteries, churches and mosques was prevented because of the existence of Allah's repelling of people, some by others. Second note:
«لولا and لو ما» are equal in urging and in being specific to verbs with «هلّا and ألّا and ألا».
There are rare exceptions for these particles that we have passed over mentioning for brevity..
2- Jihad in Islam:
The hadiths on jihad are many, among them:
On the authority of Abū Hurayra, may Allah be pleased with him: the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was asked: which deed is best? He said: "Faith in Allah and His Messenger." It was said: then what? He said: "Jihad in the way of Allah." It was said: then what? He said: "An accepted pilgrimage (ḥajj mabrūr)." Related by al-Bukhārī, Muslim, al-Tirmidhī, al-Nasāʾī and Ibn Khuzayma in his Ṣaḥīḥ.
And on the authority of Muʿādh ibn Jabal: that he asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, as they were on their way to the expedition of Tabūk, and said: "O Messenger of Allah, permit me to ask you about a matter that has made me ill and sick and sad." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Ask what you wish." He said: "O Prophet of Allah, tell me of a deed that will admit me to Paradise; I ask you about nothing else."
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Bakh, bakh, bakh, you have asked about something momentous," three times, "yet it is easy for whom Allah wills good for," repeating it three times.. He did not tell him anything without the Messenger of Allah ﷺ repeating it three times, out of eagerness that he might master it from him. Then the Prophet of Allah ﷺ said: "You believe in Allah and the Last Day.
And you establish the prayer, give the zakāt, and worship Allah alone, associating nothing with Him, until you die while you are upon that." The Messenger said: "Repeat it for me," so he repeated it three times. Then the Prophet of Allah ﷺ said: "If you wish, Muʿādh, I will tell you of the head of this matter, its pillar, and its topmost hump." Muʿādh said:
"Yes indeed, O Messenger of Allah, tell me, may my father and mother be your ransom." The Prophet of Allah ﷺ said: "The head of this matter is that you bear witness that there is no god but Allah alone, with no partner, and that Muhammad is His servant and Messenger; and that its pillar is the establishing of the prayer and the giving of the zakāt; and that its topmost hump is jihad in the way of Allah. I have only been commanded to fight the people until they establish the prayer, give the zakāt, and bear witness that there is no god but Allah.
alone, with no partner, and that Muhammad is His servant and Messenger. If they do that, they have taken hold and protected their blood and their wealth, except by its right, and their reckoning is with Allah."
And the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "By Him in whose hand is the soul of Muhammad, no face has been dust-pale and no foot has become dusty in a deed by which you seek the ranks of the Hereafter, after the obligatory prayer, like jihad in the way of Allah; and no servant's scale has become heavy like a mount that is spent in the way of Allah, or that is loaded in the way of Allah.."

safi-cedvel:42-44.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) is resumptive; (قبلهم) is an accusative adverb attached to (كذّبت), and the verb is made feminine for the meaning that "the people of Noah" carries, i.e. his tribe or his community; (قوم) is the fāʿil of كذّبت, nominative; (عاد) is conjoined to قوم by the wāw, nominative; (موسى) is the nāʾib fāʿil of the verb (كذّب), nominative, the sign of the nominative being the implied ḍamma on the alif; (الفاء) is a conjunction; (للكافرين) is attached to (أمليت); (الفاء) is resumptive; (كيف) is an interrogative noun, indeclinable, in the position of accusative, the khabar of kāna; (نكير) is the ism of kāna, nominative, the sign of the nominative being the implied ḍamma on the rāʾ because the place is occupied by the vowel of the omitted yāʾ, dropped for lightness because of the verse endings, and the omitted (ياء) is a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi.
The clause «يكذّبوك ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
The clause «كذّبت.. قوم نوح» is in the position of jussive, apodosis of the condition, joined with the fāʾ.
The clause «كذّب موسى» is in the position of jussive, conjoined to the clause كذّبت.. قوم.
The clause «أمليت ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the resumptive clause.
The clause «أخذتهم ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause أمليت.
The clause «كان نكير ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.

* Morphology:
(نكير) is a maṣdar meaning "denial" (inkār) from (نكره).. on the wazn فعيل.

safi-cedvel:45-45.t:
* I'rab:
(الفاء) is resumptive; (كأيّن) is a noun of numerical reference (kināya ʿan al-ʿadad), indeclinable, in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ «[Note: it may be a direct object of an omitted verb that the verb أهلكناها explains, its accusative then being by preoccupation (ishtighāl), and the mentioned clause explicative.]», (من قرية) is the tamyīz of كأيّن; (الواو) is circumstantial; (على عروشها) is attached to (خاوية); (الواو) is a conjunction in both places; (بئر) is conjoined to قرية, genitive «[Note: i.e. "and how many a well abandoned, from which We nullified drawing water through the death of those who drew from it, and likewise how many a palace We emptied of its inhabitants".]», and likewise (قصر).
The clause «كأيّن من قرية ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive; and the clause «أهلكناها ... » is in the position of nominative, khabar of the mubtadaʾ (كأيّن).
The clause «هي ظالمة ... » is in the position of accusative, a ḥāl from the third-person pronoun in (أهلكناها).
The clause «هي خاوية ... » is in the position of nominative, conjoined to the clause أهلكناها.

* Morphology:
(بئر) is an inert noun for the pit from which water is drawn, on the wazn فِعْل with kasra then sukūn, in the sense of the passive, like dhibḥ; it is taken from baʾara l-arḍa, i.e. he dug it.
(معطّلة) is the feminine of معطّل, the passive participle of the quadriliteral verb عطّل, on the wazn مفعّل with ḍamma on the mīm and fatḥa on the ʿayn.
(مشيد) is a passive participle from شاد يشيد, containing a weak-letter change by deletion of the wāw of mafʿūl: its origin is مشيود, then the yāʾ was made quiescent and its vowel moved to the shīn, so two quiescent letters met and the wāw was dropped; then the shīn was given kasra to suit the yāʾ, and it became مشيد, its wazn being مفعل, with fatḥa on the mīm, kasra on the fāʾ and sukūn on the ʿayn.

* Benefits:
- وَبِئْرٍ مُعَطَّلَةٍ وَقَصْرٍ مَشِيدٍ:
There are two sayings about the well and the palace referred to. One of them: that they are specific; it is related that the Prophet of Allah Ṣāliḥ came down at this well with four thousand men of those who believed with him, whom Allah the Exalted had saved from the punishment. They built a town for themselves and stayed in it for a time, then disbelieved and worshipped idols, and killed the messenger of Allah who was sent to them, so Allah destroyed them, abandoned their well and ruined their palaces.
The second: that this well and that palace are general, i.e. how many a town I destroyed, and how many a well We abandoned, and how many a lofty palace its inhabitants dispersed from.
